At the company, your workplace trainer (praktijkopleider) helps you. At school, your placement coach (stagebegeleider) helps you. Sick? Call the company before your start time, and tell the school too. Rules differ per school: ask your placement coach.
gloss.c.placement.p: I only start when the placement agreement is signed.
gloss.c.placement.s: The company asks you to start tomorrow. The POK is not signed yet. What do you do?
gloss.c.placement.o1: Ask your placement coach to arrange the POK first.
gloss.c.placement.o2: Start tomorrow, and sign the POK when you have time.
gloss.c.placement.o3: Start, but do not tell the school about it yet.
gloss.c.placement.w: The POK says what you learn and who helps you. Without a signed POK, your placement may not count for your diploma. So you sign it before you start.
gloss.c.review: Ask for feedback, and for an example
gloss.c.review.b: At your placement, people tell you what goes well and what can be better: feedback. That is normal, and it helps you learn. You do not understand it? Ask for an example. Ask for feedback yourself too, for example once a week. Is something really wrong at your placement? First talk to your workplace trainer. Does that not help? Then go to your placement coach at school.
gloss.c.review.p: What went well, and what can be better?
gloss.c.review.s: Your workplace trainer says: "You must work more carefully." You do not know what they mean. What do you do?
gloss.c.review.o1: Ask for an example of what you must do differently.
gloss.c.review.o2: Say yes, and hope that you find out yourself.
gloss.c.review.o3: Work much slower from now on, so that nothing goes wrong.
gloss.c.review.w: With an example, you know what to change. Asking shows that you want to learn. Trainers like that.
gloss.c.council.b: In the Netherlands you choose who decides, by voting. The gemeenteraad decides about your town. The Tweede Kamer makes the laws for the whole country. With Dutch nationality, you may vote in every election, from 18. More people may vote for the gemeenteraad. People from another EU country who live here may vote. People from outside the EU may vote after 5 years of legal stay. The gemeente sends you a voting pass (stempas). Bring it with your ID. Not sure if you may vote? Ask the gemeente.
gloss.c.council.p: May I vote for the gemeenteraad?
gloss.c.council.s: You come from Morocco and have lived here legally for six years. You do not have Dutch nationality. There is an election for the gemeenteraad. What is true?
gloss.c.council.o1: You may vote for the gemeenteraad.
gloss.c.council.o2: You may vote for the Tweede Kamer too.
gloss.c.council.o3: You may not vote at all without a Dutch passport.
gloss.c.council.w: After 5 years of legal stay, you may vote for the gemeenteraad. For the Tweede Kamer, you need Dutch nationality.
gloss.c.police.b: From 14, you must show your ID when the police ask for it. So always carry it with you. Did you get a letter from the gemeente or the UWV, for example? Do you not agree with the decision in it? Then you can object (bezwaar maken) in writing. Do it before the date in the letter. The police and the judge must treat everyone equally. Arrested? You may ask for a lawyer. The Juridisch Loket gives free advice.
gloss.c.police.p: I do not agree with this decision. I am objecting.
gloss.c.police.s: You get a letter from the gemeente. You do not agree with their decision. The letter says you have six weeks. What do you do?
gloss.c.police.o1: Write a letter to object, before the date.
gloss.c.police.o2: Call them once, and wait until they call you back.
gloss.c.police.o3: Wait: after six weeks, it stops by itself.
gloss.c.police.w: You object in writing, before the date in the letter. After that date, it is often too late. The Juridisch Loket can help you write it.
gloss.c.login.b: Your password and your DigiD are only for you. Do not give them to anyone, also not to your employer or a colleague. On a shared computer, always log out when you are done. Going away for a moment? Lock your screen. Forgot your password? Ask the IT department (ICT-afdeling) for a new one. Computer rules differ per company: ask the IT department what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.login.p: I am going away for a moment. I am locking my screen.
gloss.c.login.s: Your supervisor asks for your DigiD and password, to arrange your papers quickly. What do you do?
gloss.c.login.o1: Say no, and log in yourself while they help.
gloss.c.login.o2: Give it this one time, because it is your boss.
gloss.c.login.o3: Write it on a paper, so they can use it later.
gloss.c.login.w: With your DigiD, someone can see and change your tax, benefits and health papers. It is only for you. You can log in yourself and let someone help you.
gloss.c.phish: In a hurry, with a button? Do not click
gloss.c.phish.b: A fake e-mail (phishing) often looks real. It wants you to act fast: "Your account will be closed today!" Check the sender. Do not click on a link or open an attachment you did not expect. Go to the real website or app yourself. Did you click anyway? Change your password right away, and call the IT department. That is not a shame: the sooner they know, the better. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.phish.p: I clicked on a suspicious link.
gloss.c.phish.s: You clicked on a link in an e-mail and typed your password. Then you see that the e-mail was fake. What do you do?
gloss.c.phish.o1: Change your password, and call the IT department.
gloss.c.phish.o2: Delete the e-mail, so that nobody else clicks on it.
gloss.c.phish.o3: Wait a day to see if something goes wrong.
gloss.c.phish.w: With your password, someone else can get into the systems of your work. When you change it fast and tell the IT department, they can stop it in time.
gloss.c.mychoice.b: What are you good at? Think of work, school and home. Caring for family, a side job or volunteer work count too. What do you like, and what do you not like? Not sure what work fits you? Ask to join someone at work for a day (meeloopdag). Your coach at school can help you choose.
gloss.c.mychoice.p: I get on well with people. I help a lot at home.
gloss.c.mychoice.s: At school they ask: "What are you good at?" You never had a paid job. What do you say?
gloss.c.mychoice.o1: What you do well at home, like caring for others.
gloss.c.mychoice.o2: That you do not know yet, because you never had a job.
gloss.c.mychoice.o3: That you can do every kind of work, all of it.
gloss.c.mychoice.w: Skills from home count too. Caring, planning and helping are skills that employers need. Say what you did, with an example.
gloss.c.nextstep.b: With an Entree diploma, you may go on to level 2 of the mbo. A diploma at level 2 or higher is a basic qualification (startkwalificatie). It helps you to find work and to keep it. In the bbl you work at a company and go to school about one day a week. For that you need a job or a work-and-learn place (leerwerkbaan). Go to an open day, and talk to your coach at school.
gloss.c.nextstep.p: Can I go to level 2 after Entree?
gloss.c.nextstep.s: You have your Entree diploma. A company offers you a job without training. You also want to keep learning. What do you do?
gloss.c.nextstep.o1: Ask the company if a bbl place is possible.
gloss.c.nextstep.o2: Take the job, and stop learning for good.
gloss.c.nextstep.o3: Stay at home until a school calls you.
gloss.c.nextstep.w: With the bbl, you work and learn at the same time. You earn money, and you get a level 2 diploma. Many companies like this.
gloss.c.email: A short e-mail: who, what, when
gloss.c.email.b: An e-mail to work is short and polite. Start with a greeting, like "Beste Karin,". Then say what you want, and when. End with a greeting and your full name. Write a short subject, like "Vrij op vrijdag". Read your e-mail again before you send it.
gloss.c.email.p: Dear Karin, may I have Friday off? Regards, Ali Haddad
gloss.c.email.s: You want a day off next Friday. Which e-mail to your supervisor is best?
gloss.c.email.o1: "Beste Karin, mag ik vrijdag vrij? Groet, Ali Haddad"
gloss.c.email.o2: "Vrijdag ben ik er niet." (without a greeting or your name).
gloss.c.email.o3: A long e-mail about your week, with the question at the end.
gloss.c.email.w: A good e-mail has a greeting, one clear question and your name. Then your supervisor can answer quickly.
gloss.c.budget.b: When you get your pay, first pay the fixed costs: rent, insurance and your phone. Try to save a small amount every month, also 10 euros. Buy now, pay later is also a debt. Did you buy something online? Then you can usually change your mind within 14 days. Keep the receipt: you need it for the guarantee.
gloss.c.budget.p: I prefer to pay now. Then I have no debt.
gloss.c.budget.s: You get your pay today. You want new shoes, and your rent must still be paid. What do you do?
gloss.c.budget.o1: Pay the rent first, then see what is left.
gloss.c.budget.o2: Buy the shoes, and pay the rent later.
gloss.c.budget.o3: Buy the shoes with buy now, pay later.
gloss.c.budget.w: Rent, insurance and your phone come back every month. When you pay those first, you know what money is left. Then you do not get debts.
gloss.c.healthy.b: You work better and more safely when you sleep enough, also after a late shift. Eat breakfast, and drink water during the day. Move in your break, for example a short walk. Working under the influence of alcohol or drugs is dangerous, and most employers forbid it. Do you feel low for a long time, or can you not stop drinking or using? Talk to your huisarts. They can help, and they keep it secret.
gloss.c.healthy.p: I have felt low for a long time. Can I make an appointment?
gloss.c.healthy.s: You have a night shift tonight. A colleague offers you a pill to stay awake. What do you do?
gloss.c.healthy.o1: Say no, and sleep a few hours before your shift.
gloss.c.healthy.o2: Take half a pill, that is not dangerous.
gloss.c.healthy.o3: Take it, but tell nobody at work about it.
gloss.c.healthy.w: Pills from a colleague can be drugs. They can make you sick, or make you make mistakes at work. Sleep is the safe way to stay awake.
gloss.w.inladen: to load (put things into the van)
gloss.w.bewijs: the proof (something that shows what happened)
gloss.s.parcel.2: The customer is not at home.
gloss.s.parcel.3: Would you take in a parcel for the neighbours?
gloss.c.parcel.a: Yes. Would you sign here, please?
gloss.l.road: Safe and fair on the road
gloss.w.steekwagen: the hand truck (a trolley for heavy boxes)
gloss.w.loondienst: employed (you work for a boss and get a wage)
gloss.w.bepalen: to decide (say how it must be done)
gloss.s.road.1: This parcel is too heavy. I am getting the hand truck.
gloss.s.road.2: It is slippery. I am driving slowly.
gloss.s.road.3: Who decides my route and my times?
gloss.c.road.q: Can you do one more run today?
gloss.c.road.a: No, then I have no time for my break.
gloss.c.parcel: Not at home, or a broken parcel
gloss.c.parcel.b: Is the customer not at home? Follow the rules of your company: try the neighbours, or take the parcel back. Do not just leave it at the door, unless the customer asked for that. Is a parcel broken or wet? Do not deliver it as if nothing is wrong. Take a photo as proof, and report it in the scanner or the app. Being honest about a problem is always better than hiding it. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.parcel.p: This parcel is broken. Here is a photo.
gloss.c.parcel.s: The customer is not at home, and the neighbours are not either. What do you do?
gloss.c.parcel.o1: Scan "not at home", and take it back.
gloss.c.parcel.o2: Scan it as delivered, and leave it at the door.
gloss.c.parcel.o3: Hide it behind the bin, so nobody sees it.
gloss.c.parcel.w: A parcel scanned as delivered must really be with the customer. When you scan what really happened, the customer can get the parcel later, and nobody thinks you lost it.
gloss.c.road: Safe on the road, and fair work
gloss.c.road.b: Never hold your phone while you drive: that is forbidden. Use a holder for the navigation. Take your breaks, also on a busy day. A heavy parcel? Use the hand truck, or lift it together. Ice or snow? Drive slowly: arriving late is better than an accident. Some companies say you work as self-employed (zelfstandig). But who decides your hours, your route and your clothes? If the company decides all that, you may be an employee after all (in loondienst). Then you often have more rights, like pay when you are sick. More about this in the lesson "Papers, integration and your job". General information. For your situation: ask the union, the Juridisch Loket or FairWork.
gloss.c.road.p: I am taking my break now. Then I will drive on.
gloss.c.road.s: The company calls you self-employed. But it decides your hours, your route and your clothes. What do you do?
gloss.c.road.o1: Ask for advice: maybe you are an employee.
gloss.c.road.o2: Nothing: the contract says self-employed, so it is.
gloss.c.road.o3: Work more hours, so you earn the same.
gloss.c.road.w: What counts is how you really work, not only the word on the contract. If the company decides how, when and where you work, you are often an employee. Then you have more rights.
gloss.s.mustmay.1: Do I have to sign this?
gloss.s.mustmay.2: No, you do not have to sign.
gloss.s.mustmay.3: That is the rule: a helmet is compulsory.
gloss.c.mustmay.q: Do I have to work overtime on Saturday?
gloss.c.mustmay.a: No, that is not necessary. It is voluntary.
gloss.c.mustmay.b: In Dutch, the opposite of "moeten" is "niet hoeven". "Je moet tekenen" means: you have no choice. "Je hoeft niet te tekenen" means: you may choose. "Je mag niet tekenen" means: it is forbidden. Careful: in English, "must not" means "mag niet". In many languages, "not must" means "hoeft niet". Not sure? Ask it.
gloss.c.mustmay.p: Do I have to, or do I have a choice?
gloss.c.mustmay.s: Your team leader says: "Je hoeft zaterdag niet te komen." What does he mean?
gloss.c.mustmay.o1: You do not have to come on Saturday. You may choose.
gloss.c.mustmay.o2: You are not allowed to come on Saturday.
gloss.c.mustmay.w: "Niet hoeven" means it is not compulsory: you may choose. "Niet mogen" would mean it is forbidden.
gloss.w.waterpas: the spirit level (it shows if something is straight)
gloss.c.measure.a: Ninety centimetres. I am writing it down.
gloss.c.measure.b: On a building site, measures are often in millimetres. So "nine hundred" can mean 90 centimetres. Not sure? Ask: "Is that millimetres or centimetres?" Say the number back, and write it down. Measure twice before you saw or drill: a plank that is too short stays too short. Did you make a mistake? Say it right away. Then the team can still fix it, and it costs less.
gloss.c.measure.p: Is that in millimetres or in centimetres?
gloss.c.measure.s: Your colleague calls a measure. You did not hear it well. What do you do?
gloss.c.measure.o1: Say the number back, and ask if it is right.
gloss.c.measure.o2: Saw the plank at what you think you heard.
gloss.c.measure.o3: Wait until he comes to look himself.
gloss.c.measure.w: A wrong measure costs material and time. Saying the number back takes two seconds, and everyone on a building site does it.
gloss.w.uitvoerder: the site manager (the boss on the building site)
gloss.w.keet: the site cabin (for breaks and meetings)
gloss.w.container: the skip (a very big bin for waste)
gloss.s.siteday.1: The waste goes in the skip.
gloss.s.siteday.2: The site manager is in the cabin.
gloss.c.siteday.a: In the skip at the entrance.
gloss.c.siteday: A tidy site is a safe site
gloss.c.siteday.b: On a building site, tidying up is part of the job, for everyone. Loose planks, cables and waste make people trip and fall. So clear your own place during the day, not only at the end. Waste is sorted: wood, stone and metal often go in different skips. Not sure which one? Ask. Do you see a nail sticking out, or a hole without a cover? Fix it if you can do that safely, or tell the site manager (de uitvoerder). Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.siteday.p: I will clear this up. Then nobody trips.
gloss.c.siteday.s: Planks with nails lie on the path. They are not yours. What do you do?
gloss.c.siteday.o1: Move them aside, or tell the site manager.
gloss.c.siteday.o2: Step over them: they are not your planks.
gloss.c.siteday.o3: Wait: someone else will clear them.
gloss.c.siteday.w: Everyone uses the same paths. Who sees a danger, does something about it: that is normal on a building site.
gloss.w.overdracht: the handover (you tell the next shift what happened)
gloss.w.aflossen: to take over from (the next person comes, and you can go)
gloss.s.shifts.1: I have the late shift this week.
gloss.c.shifts.q: Did anything happen in your shift?
gloss.c.shifts.a: Yes. The line stood still for half an hour.
gloss.c.shifts.b: A factory often runs day and night, in shifts. At the end of your shift, a colleague takes over your place. Do not just leave: wait until your colleague is there. Tell in a few words what happened: a fault, a product that was wrong, something that is not finished. Many companies also have a list or a screen for this. A problem you do not pass on comes back in the next shift, and then nobody knows why. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.shifts.p: The machine had a fault. Now it works again.
gloss.c.shifts.s: Your shift is over. Your colleague is five minutes late. What do you do?
gloss.c.shifts.o1: Wait, and tell the team leader.
gloss.c.shifts.o2: Go home: your shift is over.
gloss.c.shifts.w: A running machine may not stand alone. When you wait and report it, the work goes on safely, and the team leader can solve it.
gloss.w.misselijk: sick (you feel you must throw up)
gloss.w.verward: confused (the person does not know where they are)
gloss.s.signals.2: The gentleman is not eating today.
gloss.s.signals.3: Can you come and have a look?
gloss.c.signals.a: He is confused. That is different from yesterday.
gloss.c.signals: You see the client every day
gloss.c.signals.b: You are often the one who sees a client the most. So you notice it first when something is different: eating less, more pain, confused, short of breath. You do not have to know what it is. Say what you see, and say when you saw it. Tell the nurse the same day, and write it down if that is your task. Does it look serious? Do not wait: call the nurse right away. Better one time too many than one time too few.
gloss.c.signals.p: The lady is not eating and is dizzy. That is different from normal.
gloss.c.signals.s: A client is quiet today and does not want to eat. Normally she talks a lot. What do you do?
gloss.c.signals.o1: Tell the nurse what you see, today.
gloss.c.signals.o2: Wait a few days: maybe it passes.
gloss.c.signals.o3: Give her a pill from the cupboard.
gloss.c.signals.w: A small change can be the first sign of an illness. You do not decide what it is: the nurse does. But she can only act if you tell her.
gloss.w.tillift: the hoist (a machine that lifts a person)
gloss.w.opstaan: to get up, to stand up
gloss.s.transfer.1: I will help you get up.
gloss.s.transfer.2: Would you like to sit down for a moment?
gloss.s.transfer.3: First I will get the hoist.
gloss.c.transfer.q: Can you lift the lady out of bed?
gloss.c.transfer.a: Not on my own. I will get the hoist.
gloss.c.transfer.b: Before you touch a client, say what you are going to do: "Ik help u nu met opstaan." Then the client is not startled, and can help along. Let the client do what they can still do: that keeps them strong. Do not lift a person on your own. Use the aids that are there, like the hoist, and work the way you were shown. Not shown yet? Ask first. Your back must last a whole working life. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.transfer.p: I will help you get up now. Are you ready?
gloss.c.transfer.s: A client wants to get out of bed. You have not learned to use the hoist yet. What do you do?
gloss.c.transfer.o1: Ask a colleague who knows the hoist.
gloss.c.transfer.o2: Lift her yourself: she is not heavy.
gloss.c.transfer.o3: Try the hoist: it cannot be hard.
gloss.c.transfer.w: Lifting a person the wrong way can hurt the client and your back. Asking a colleague takes a few minutes. A fall can take months.
gloss.s.dishes.3: There is no clean cutlery left.
gloss.c.dishes.q: Are there any clean glasses left?
gloss.c.dishes.a: Yes, I will bring them right away.
gloss.c.dishes: Broken glass: say it right away
gloss.c.dishes.b: In a kitchen, glass breaks. That is normal, and nobody is angry about it. But say it right away, loud and clear: "Glas!" Do not pick up the pieces with your bare hands: use a brush. Did glass fall near food, or in the ice? Then that food or that ice must be thrown away, all of it. A small piece of glass in a meal is very dangerous for a guest. Glass goes in its own bin, not in a bag that someone lifts. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.dishes.p: Careful, glass! I will clear it up right away.
gloss.c.dishes.s: A glass breaks above the ice for the drinks. It is very busy. What do you do?
gloss.c.dishes.o1: Say it, and throw away all the ice.
gloss.c.dishes.o2: Take out the pieces you can see.
gloss.c.dishes.o3: Say nothing: it is too busy now.
gloss.c.dishes.w: You cannot see small pieces of glass in ice. New ice costs little. A guest with glass in a drink can get badly hurt.
gloss.w.chef: the chef (the boss of the kitchen)
gloss.s.rush.1: Hot! I am passing behind you.
gloss.s.rush.2: Table six is waiting for the food.
gloss.s.rush.3: I am taking this to the terrace.
gloss.c.rush: Short words when it is busy
gloss.c.rush.b: When it is busy, people in a kitchen talk in short words: "Heet!", "Achter!", "Tafel zes!" That is not rude. It is fast and safe: everyone knows where the hot pans and the knives are. Call "Heet!" or "Achter!" yourself when you pass behind someone. Did you hear an order? Say it back: "Ja, chef." Then the chef knows you heard it. Was someone short with you in the rush? Often that is over after the service. Does it stay unpleasant? Then talk about it at a quiet moment.
gloss.c.rush.p: Behind! I have a hot pan.
gloss.c.rush.s: It is very busy. The chef calls: "Tafel zes, nu!" He does not say please. What do you do?
gloss.c.rush.o2: Stop, and say that he is rude.
gloss.c.rush.o3: Do it, but say nothing back.
gloss.c.rush.w: In the rush, short is normal and not meant personally. Saying it back shows that you heard it. That keeps the kitchen fast and safe.
gloss.w.verdieping: the floor (the 1st or 2nd floor of a building)
gloss.s.rounds.1: I start on the second floor.
gloss.s.rounds.2: The toilet paper has run out.
gloss.c.rounds.q: Have you done office three yet?
gloss.c.rounds.a: No, someone is still working there.
gloss.c.rounds.b: Often you clean while other people are still at work. Greet them, and ask: "Mag ik hier even schoonmaken?" Most people say yes. Is someone in a meeting or on the phone? Then come back later. Do not move papers on a desk, and do not read them: clean around them. You have a set time for your round. Is the time too short to do it well? Do not skip rooms in silence. Tell your supervisor what you could not do, and why.
gloss.c.rounds.p: Good afternoon. May I clean here for a moment?
gloss.c.rounds.s: Your round takes longer today: one room was very dirty. Two offices are not done. What do you do?
gloss.c.rounds.o1: Tell your supervisor which two, and why.
gloss.c.rounds.o2: Go home, and hope nobody sees it.
gloss.c.rounds.o3: Do them very fast, without the floors.
gloss.c.rounds.w: A customer who finds a dirty office complains. A supervisor who knows about it can explain it, or give you more time. Telling it is not failing.
gloss.s.colours.1: The red cloth is for the toilet.
gloss.s.colours.3: Which colour do I use here?
gloss.c.colours.q: May I use this cloth for the desk?
gloss.c.colours.a: No, the red one is only for the toilet.
gloss.c.colours.b: Many cleaning companies work with colours. Each colour of cloth, sponge and bucket is for one place. Often red is for the toilet, and blue is for desks and tables. This way, dirt from the toilet does not get onto a desk or into a kitchen. The colours can be different at each company, so ask on your first day. Is a cloth dirty, or did it fall on the floor? Take a clean one. Used cloths go in the laundry bag, not back on the cart. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.colours.p: Which colour is for the toilet here?
gloss.c.colours.s: Your blue cloths are finished. You must still clean three desks. You only have red cloths. What do you do?
gloss.c.colours.o2: Use a red cloth: clean is clean.
gloss.c.colours.o3: Use one blue cloth again for all three.
gloss.c.colours.w: A colour system only works when everyone always follows it. Then nobody has to wonder where a cloth has been.
gloss.w.aanbieding: the special offer (cheaper for a short time)
gloss.s.shophelp.2: Would you like a bag with it?
gloss.s.shophelp.3: This coffee is on special offer.
gloss.c.shophelp.q: Do you have any milk left?
gloss.c.shophelp.a: I will have a look in the stockroom for you.
gloss.c.shophelp: "I do not know" is not the end
gloss.c.shophelp.b: A customer asks something and you do not know the answer. That is fine: nobody knows everything. But do not say only "nee" or "weet ik niet", and do not walk away. Say: "Ik vraag het even voor u", and get a colleague. Is a product sold out? Say when it comes in again, or show something like it. Look at the customer and greet them, also when you are busy stocking shelves. Did you not understand the question? Ask the customer to say it again, slowly.
gloss.c.shophelp.p: I do not know that. I will ask for you.
gloss.c.shophelp.s: A customer asks for a product. You do not know the word. What do you do?
gloss.c.shophelp.o1: Say: "Ik vraag het even voor u."
gloss.c.shophelp.o3: Point somewhere, so she walks away.
gloss.c.shophelp.w: A customer does not mind that you are new or still learning Dutch. A customer does mind getting no help. Getting a colleague is good service.
gloss.s.shoptrouble.1: I will get the store manager.
gloss.s.shoptrouble.3: I think someone is stealing something.
gloss.c.shoptrouble.q: I want my money back now!
gloss.c.shoptrouble.a: I understand. I will get my colleague.
gloss.c.shoptrouble: An angry customer or a thief: you come first
gloss.c.shoptrouble.b: Sometimes a customer gets angry, or you see someone stealing. Your safety comes first, always. With an angry customer: stay calm, do not shout back, and get the store manager. You do not have to solve it alone. Do you see a thief? Do not run after them, do not hold them, and do not block the door. Look well at what you see, and tell the manager or the security guard right away. Things can be replaced. You cannot. Were you scared afterwards? Talk about it with your supervisor. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.shoptrouble.p: I see someone putting something in his bag.
gloss.c.shoptrouble.s: A man puts a bottle under his coat and walks to the exit. What do you do?
gloss.c.shoptrouble.o1: Tell the manager or the guard.
gloss.c.shoptrouble.o2: Run after him and hold his arm.
gloss.c.shoptrouble.o3: Stand in front of the door.
gloss.c.shoptrouble.w: A thief who is stopped can get violent. The manager and the guard know what to do. No product is worth getting hurt for.
gloss.s.plantcare.1: This tomato is not ripe yet.
gloss.s.plantcare.2: I am cutting the leaf away.
gloss.c.plantcare.a: Only the red ones. The green ones are not ripe yet.
gloss.c.plantcare.b: Plants can get sick too. A virus goes from plant to plant on hands, gloves, knives and clothes. In a greenhouse, one sick plant can mean that thousands of plants must go. That is why there are strict rules at the door: wash your hands, wear the work clothes of the company, and walk through the foot bath. Many greenhouses do not allow your own tomatoes, peppers or cucumbers in your lunch. Do you see a plant that looks strange? Do not touch it. Tell your supervisor which row it is. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.plantcare.p: There is a sick plant in row twelve.
gloss.c.plantcare.s: You see a plant with strange yellow spots. What do you do?
gloss.c.plantcare.o1: Leave it, and tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.plantcare.o2: Pull it out and take it with you.
gloss.c.plantcare.o3: Cut off the leaves with spots.
gloss.c.plantcare.w: When you touch a sick plant, the virus goes with you to the next plants. Your supervisor knows how to take it away safely.
gloss.w.regenpak: the rain suit (a jacket and trousers against rain)
gloss.s.outdoors.1: It is raining. I am putting on my rain suit.
gloss.c.outdoors.q: A thunderstorm is coming. What do we do?
gloss.c.outdoors.b: Outside, you work in all kinds of weather. In the sun: cover your head and your skin, use sunscreen, and drink water often. In the rain: wear your rain suit and boots, and put on dry clothes in your break. Wet and cold make you sick and slow. Is there thunder? Then stop and go inside, or into a car or a van. Not under a tree, and not in an open field. Do you need rain clothes or boots for the work? Ask your employer about them before you buy them yourself.
gloss.c.outdoors.p: There is going to be thunder. Shall we go inside?
gloss.c.outdoors.s: You are on the field. You hear thunder nearby. Your row is almost finished. What do you do?
gloss.c.outdoors.o1: Stop, and go inside or into the van.
gloss.c.outdoors.w: Lightning hits the highest point, and on a flat field that is you. The row can wait a quarter of an hour.
gloss.w.tekening: the drawing (it shows how the part must be)
gloss.s.drawing.1: What is the measure on the drawing?
gloss.s.drawing.3: It is two millimetres too big.
gloss.c.drawing.a: No. I will measure it one more time.
gloss.c.drawing.b: In a workshop you make what the drawing says, not what looks about right. The measures are in millimetres, and one millimetre can be too much. Does a part not fit? Do not use force, and do not make the hole bigger "just a little". Measure again, and look at the drawing. Can you not read the drawing, or is a measure missing? Ask before you start. A question costs a minute. A wrong part costs material and hours.
gloss.c.drawing.p: I cannot read this measure. Can you have a look?
gloss.c.drawing.s: A part does not fit: it is one millimetre too big. With a hammer it would go in. What do you do?
gloss.c.drawing.o1: Measure again, and ask what to do.
gloss.c.drawing.o2: Hit it in with the hammer.
gloss.c.drawing.o3: Grind a bit off, and say nothing.
gloss.c.drawing.w: A part that goes in with force can break later, at the customer. When you report it, the cause can be found.
gloss.w.lassen: to weld (join metal with great heat)
gloss.w.afzuiging: the extraction (it takes the smoke away)
gloss.s.weld.1: I am putting on my welding helmet.
gloss.s.weld.3: Careful, the metal is still hot.
gloss.c.weld.q: May I pick this up already?
gloss.c.weld.a: No, wait. It must cool down first.
gloss.c.weld.b: Welding gives very bright light. Do not look into it without a welding helmet, also not from a distance: your eyes can burn, and you feel it only hours later. Is a colleague welding near you? Look away, or stand behind the screen. Metal that was just welded or ground looks normal, but it is very hot. Do not pick it up with bare hands. Welding smoke is bad for your lungs: switch on the extraction. A burn? Cool it with water right away, for at least ten minutes, and report it. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.weld.s: A colleague is welding next to you. You have no welding helmet on. What do you do?
gloss.c.weld.o1: Look away, and stand behind the screen.
gloss.c.weld.o2: Watch for a moment: you can learn from it.
gloss.c.weld.w: The light of welding burns your eyes, also from the side and from a distance. You feel the pain only later, often at night.
gloss.w.motorkap: the bonnet (the cover over the engine)
gloss.s.carparts.2: The front left light is broken.
gloss.c.carparts.a: The engine makes a strange sound.
gloss.c.carparts: The car belongs to the customer
gloss.c.carparts.b: A car in the garage is not yours: it is the customer’s. Put a cover on the seat and on the steering wheel before you get in, and work with clean hands inside. Leave the seat, the mirrors and the radio the way they were. Did you have to move the seat? Put it back. Do not touch personal things in the car. Did you make a scratch or a stain? Tell your supervisor right away. A customer who finds it at home does not come back.
gloss.c.carparts.p: I made a scratch. I am sorry.
gloss.c.carparts.s: You make a small scratch on a customer’s car door. Nobody saw it. What do you do?
gloss.c.carparts.o2: Say nothing: it is very small.
gloss.c.carparts.o3: Rub it away with a cloth, and hope.
gloss.c.carparts.w: Everyone makes a mistake sometimes. A garage can repair a scratch, or tell the customer honestly. A hidden scratch costs the garage its good name.
gloss.w.krik: the jack (it lifts one side of the car)
gloss.w.lap: the rag (a cloth for dirty work)
gloss.s.carsafe.2: Oil has been spilled. I am getting a rag.
gloss.s.carsafe.3: I do not touch the orange cables.
gloss.c.carsafe.q: May I work on this car?
gloss.c.carsafe.a: Not yet. It is an electric car.
gloss.c.carsafe.b: An electric or hybrid car has a battery with very high power. The cables for it are orange. Do not touch or loosen them: a mechanic with special training must make the car safe first. Is there a sign or a cone at the car? Then stay away. An engine that runs inside makes a gas that you cannot smell or see, and it can kill. So: put the exhaust hose on, or open the doors. Do you smell petrol? No sparks and no smoking. Tell your supervisor right away. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.carsafe.p: Has this car been made safe yet?
gloss.c.carsafe.s: You must change a wheel on an electric car. Under the car you see a loose orange cable. What do you do?
gloss.c.carsafe.o1: Touch nothing, and get the trained mechanic.
gloss.c.carsafe.o2: Push the cable back with your hand.
gloss.c.carsafe.o3: Push it back with a dry cloth.
gloss.c.carsafe.w: The battery of an electric car has enough power to kill, also when the car is off. Only someone with the training may touch these parts.
gloss.w.tanken: to fill up (put fuel in the van)
gloss.w.opladen: to charge (an electric van, a phone)
gloss.s.vancheck.1: There is a dent in the door.
gloss.s.vancheck.3: I still have to fill up first.
gloss.c.vancheck.q: Is everything fine with the van?
gloss.c.vancheck.b: Walk around the van before your first run. Do you see a dent, a scratch or a broken mirror? Take a photo, and report it before you drive away. Then everyone knows the damage was already there. Did something happen during your run? Report it the same day, also when it is small. Hiding damage gives bigger problems later. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.vancheck.p: There is damage on the van. Here is a photo.
gloss.c.vancheck.s: In the morning you see a new dent in the van. You did not make it. What do you do?
gloss.c.vancheck.o1: Take a photo, and report it before you drive.
gloss.c.vancheck.o2: Say nothing: it is not your dent.
gloss.c.vancheck.o3: Wait and see if someone asks about it.
gloss.c.vancheck.w: When you report it before you drive, nobody can think you did it. A photo with the time is clear for everyone.
gloss.w.vertraging: the delay (you are later than planned)
gloss.w.omleiding: the diversion (another road, because the road is closed)
gloss.w.navigatie: the navigation (the app that shows the way)
gloss.w.planner: the planner (the person who makes the routes)
gloss.w.retour: the return (a parcel that goes back)
gloss.s.delay.1: I am in a traffic jam.
gloss.s.delay.2: I have a delay of half an hour.
gloss.c.delay.a: At the diversion. I will be ten minutes later.
gloss.c.delay.b: A traffic jam or a closed road is not your fault. But tell the planner as soon as you know that you will be late. Then the planner can tell the customers, or change the route. Stop in a safe place first: do not call with the phone in your hand while you drive. And do not drive faster to win back the time. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.delay.p: I am in a traffic jam. I will be half an hour later.
gloss.c.delay.s: A road is closed. The diversion costs you thirty minutes. What do you do?
gloss.c.delay.o1: Tell the planner as soon as you can stop safely.
gloss.c.delay.o2: Drive faster, so you win back the lost time.
gloss.c.delay.w: When the planner knows it early, the customers hear it and nobody waits for nothing. Driving faster is dangerous, and it wins almost no time.
gloss.w.zetten: to put (something that stands: a box, a bucket)
gloss.w.leggen: to put, to lay (something that lies flat)
gloss.w.brengen: to bring, to take (to a place or a person)
gloss.c.putdown.q: Can you hold this for a moment?
gloss.c.putdown.a: Yes. Where must I put it?
gloss.c.putdown.b: Do you carry something together, or does a colleague hand you something heavy? Say "Ik heb hem" when you hold it well. Then your colleague knows that it is safe to let go. Do you want to let go yourself? Ask first: "Heb je hem?" And wait for the answer. This is normal on every work floor. It keeps things from falling on feet and hands.
gloss.c.putdown.p: I have it. You can let go.
gloss.c.putdown.s: A colleague hands you a heavy box. You do not hold it well yet. What do you do?
gloss.c.putdown.o1: Say "wacht", and hold it better first.
gloss.c.putdown.o2: Say nothing: he will see it.
gloss.c.putdown.o3: Take it fast, so he does not wait.
gloss.c.putdown.w: Your colleague lets go when he thinks that you have it. One word gives you the time to hold it well.
gloss.l.onoff: On and off, open and closed
gloss.c.onoff.a: No. I am closing it now.
gloss.c.onoff.b: Does someone call "Stop!"? Stop at once, also when you do not know why. Ask afterwards. A short, loud word is not anger here: it is how colleagues keep each other safe. Do you see something dangerous yourself? Call "Stop!" too, also to someone who has worked here for years. Nobody finds that strange.
gloss.c.onoff.s: You switch a machine on. A colleague calls "Stop!". You do not see a problem. What do you do?
gloss.c.onoff.o1: Stop at once, and ask why afterwards.
gloss.c.onoff.o2: Go on: you do not see a problem.
gloss.c.onoff.o3: Ask first why you must stop.
gloss.c.onoff.w: Your colleague may see something that you do not see. First stop, then talk: that keeps everyone safe.
gloss.s.fillempty.2: This one is full. Empty it.
gloss.c.fillempty.b: Are you done with a task? Say it: "Ik ben klaar." And ask what you can do next. Waiting quietly until someone sees you can look as if you do not want to work, also when that is not true. Colleagues who ask for the next task often get more interesting work after a while. Do you want to learn something new? Ask that too: "Mag ik dat ook leren?"
gloss.c.fillempty.p: I am done. What else can I do?
gloss.c.fillempty.s: You are done with your task. Your supervisor is busy with something else. What do you do?
gloss.c.fillempty.o1: Say that you are done, and ask what is next.
gloss.c.fillempty.o2: Wait until your supervisor sees you.
gloss.c.fillempty.o3: Take a break: your work is finished.
gloss.c.fillempty.w: A supervisor cannot see everything. When you say that you are done, the work goes on, and you show that you want to do more.
gloss.c.order: Many tasks at once? Ask what comes first
gloss.c.order.b: Sometimes you get three tasks in one sentence. That is hard to remember, also for people who speak Dutch well. Ask which one comes first: "Wat moet ik eerst doen?" You may also write the tasks down, or count them on your fingers and say them back. Did you forget one? Go back and ask. That is better than guessing.
gloss.c.order.p: That is a lot. What must I do first?
gloss.c.order.s: Your supervisor gives you three tasks, very fast. You remember only the first one. What do you do?
gloss.c.order.o1: Ask right away to hear the tasks once more.
gloss.c.order.o2: Do the first one, and hope you remember the rest.
gloss.c.order.o3: Do nothing: you do not know all three.
gloss.c.order.w: Asking at once costs ten seconds. Later your supervisor may be gone, and then you wait or guess.
gloss.w.lijmkam: the notched trowel (spreads tile glue in ridges)
gloss.w.nijptang: the pincers (to nip small bits off a tile)
gloss.w.mixer: the paddle mixer (stirs glue or plaster in a bucket)
gloss.s.tiletools.1: Give me the notched trowel for a moment.
gloss.s.tiletools.2: I cut the tile with the tile cutter.
gloss.s.tiletools.3: Measure with the folding ruler first.
gloss.c.tiletools.a: By the bucket, next to the door.
gloss.c.tiletools: Clean your tools before the glue is hard
gloss.c.tiletools.b: Tile glue and plaster get hard fast, also on your tools. So clean the notched trowel, the trowel and the mixer in a bucket of water right away, also before your break. Hard glue does not come off, and a notched trowel with hard glue makes bad ridges. Do not pour the dirty water into a sink or a drain: it gets blocked. Ask where the water may go. The mixer: hold it with two hands, and start it slowly. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.tiletools.p: I am just cleaning the notched trowel.
gloss.c.tiletools.s: It is time for your break. Your notched trowel is full of wet glue. What do you do?
gloss.c.tiletools.o1: Clean it in water, then take your break.
gloss.c.tiletools.o2: Leave it: you clean it after work.
gloss.c.tiletools.o3: Put it in the bucket of glue.
gloss.c.tiletools.w: Tile glue gets hard in your break too. A clean notched trowel makes good ridges, and the tiles stick well. Hard glue on it is a lot of work, or a new tool.
gloss.l.tiling: Tiles, glue and the centre line
gloss.w.tegelkruisje: the tile spacer (a small cross between the tiles)
gloss.w.hartlijn: the centre line (you start tiling from it)
gloss.w.tegelplaat: the tiling board (a board to practise setting tiles)
gloss.s.tiling.1: The tile glue is still wet.
gloss.s.tiling.2: Put a tile spacer between the tiles.
gloss.s.tiling.3: First draw the centre line with the pencil.
gloss.c.tiling.q: Where do I start with the tiles?
gloss.c.tiling.a: In the middle, on the centre line.
gloss.c.tiling: Start at the centre line, with a little glue
gloss.c.tiling.b: A tiler does not start in a corner. You draw the centre line first, with a pencil and the spirit level, and you start there. Then the cut tiles at both ends are the same size. Spread only as much glue as you can cover with tiles in a short time. Glue that stands too long gets a dry skin, and then the tiles do not stick well. Put a spacer at every crossing, so all the joints are the same. Check often with the spirit level: a crooked tile is easy to fix now, and hard to fix tomorrow.
gloss.c.tiling.p: I do not spread too much glue at once.
gloss.c.tiling.s: After a long phone call, the glue on the wall has a dry skin. What do you do?
gloss.c.tiling.o1: Scrape it off, and spread fresh glue.
gloss.c.tiling.o2: Press the tiles into it anyway.
gloss.c.tiling.o3: Make it wet with a sponge, and go on.
gloss.c.tiling.w: Glue with a dry skin does not hold a tile well. Later the tile can come loose, and then the work must be done again.
gloss.w.stucspaan: the plastering trowel (a flat steel float to smooth plaster)
gloss.w.oplegspaan: the hawk (a flat board you hold the plaster on)
gloss.w.spackmes: the filling knife (a wide flat knife)
gloss.w.rei: the straightedge (a long straight bar to level plaster)
gloss.w.hoekprofiel: the corner bead (a metal strip for a straight corner)
gloss.s.plaster.1: First put the corner bead on the corner.
gloss.s.plaster.2: Make the wall smooth with the plastering trowel.
gloss.s.plaster.3: Pull the straightedge over the wall.
gloss.c.plaster.b: Fresh plaster stays wet for a long time. A wet wall is darker than a dry one. The painter can only start when the wall is dry everywhere, and that can take days or weeks. Do not dry it faster with a heater: then the plaster can crack. Does someone want to paint too early? Say that the wall is not dry yet. And before you start, cover the floor, the windows and the sockets: plaster is hard to get off.
gloss.c.plaster.p: The wall is still wet. You cannot paint yet.
gloss.c.plaster.s: The painter wants to start tomorrow. The new plaster still has dark spots. What do you do?
gloss.c.plaster.o1: Tell the painter: the wall is not dry yet.
gloss.c.plaster.o2: Put a heater in front of it tonight.
gloss.c.plaster.o3: Say nothing: the painter will see it.
gloss.c.plaster.w: Dark spots mean that the plaster is still wet. Paint on a wet wall can come loose, and a heater can make cracks. Waiting costs less than doing it again.
gloss.w.penseel: the small brush (for corners and edges)
gloss.w.strijkvaatje: the paint kettle (a small pot you hold while painting)
gloss.s.paint.3: Put a little paint in the paint kettle.
gloss.c.paint.a: The wide one for the wall, the small brush for the corners.
gloss.c.paint: Stir well, and paint from the top down
gloss.c.paint.b: Paint that stood still for a while is thick at the bottom of the tin. So stir it well first, with a stirring stick, until the colour is the same everywhere. Do not paint from the big tin: put a little paint in the paint kettle, and close the tin again. Then the paint stays good. Paint from the top down, so drips land on wet paint and you can still brush them away. Use the wide brush for the wall and the small brush for the corners. At the end, clean the brushes right away.
gloss.c.paint.p: I stir the paint well first.
gloss.c.paint.s: You open an old tin of paint. On top it is thin, at the bottom thick. What do you do?
gloss.c.paint.o1: Stir it well first, with the stick.
gloss.c.paint.o2: Paint with the thin paint on top.
gloss.c.paint.o3: Add water until it is thin everywhere.
gloss.c.paint.w: Part of the colour sits at the bottom of the tin. Without stirring, the wall gets spots and stripes.
gloss.w.afplakken: to mask off (cover an edge with tape)
gloss.s.prep.1: First scrape off the old paint.
gloss.s.prep.3: Sweep the dust away with the small brush.
gloss.c.prep.a: No, first sand and fill the hole.
gloss.c.prep: Good paint work starts before the paint
gloss.c.prep.b: Paint does not stick well on dirt, dust or loose old paint. So first scrape the loose paint off with the paint scraper. Fill holes with filler and the putty knife, and let the filler dry. Then sand it smooth. After sanding, sweep the dust away with the small brush, also from the edges. Last, mask off what must stay clean, like windows and sockets. Sanding makes fine dust: wear a dust mask, and ask which one. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.prep.s: You sanded the door. There is still dust on it. Your colleague wants to paint now. What do you do?
gloss.c.prep.o1: Sweep the dust off first, with the brush.
gloss.c.prep.o2: Let them paint: the paint covers the dust.
gloss.c.prep.o3: Wipe the dust off with your hand.
gloss.c.prep.w: Paint on dust does not stick well. Later it comes off in flakes, and then all the work must be done again.
gloss.w.voegijzer: the jointer (to smooth the joints between bricks)
gloss.s.brick.1: There is still cement in the mortar tub.
gloss.s.brick.2: Make the joint smooth with the jointer.
gloss.s.brick.3: Brush the wall clean with the hand brush.
gloss.c.brick.q: How many bricks do you have left?
gloss.c.brick.a: One more pallet. Enough for today.
gloss.c.brick: Keep the wall clean while you work
gloss.c.brick.b: Mortar is wet when you lay the bricks, and it gets hard in a few hours. So work clean. Scrape the mortar that comes out of the joint off with the trowel right away. Smooth the joints with the jointer when the mortar is a little stiff, not when it is still wet. Then brush the wall with the hand brush. Hard mortar on the front of a brick is very hard to get off. At the end of the day, cover the top of the wall, so rain does not wash the mortar out.
gloss.c.brick.s: At the end of the day there is mortar on the front of the bricks. What do you do?
gloss.c.brick.o1: Brush it off now, before it is hard.
gloss.c.brick.o2: Leave it: you clean it next week.
gloss.c.brick.o3: Wash the wall with a lot of water.
gloss.c.brick.w: Fresh mortar comes off easily with a brush. Hard mortar stays on the brick, and then the wall does not look good.
gloss.w.metseltouw: the brick line (a string for a straight row)
gloss.w.klos: the line block (holds the string at the corner)
gloss.w.lagenmaatlat: the gauge rod (shows the height of each row)
gloss.w.profiel: the corner profile (a straight post at the end of the wall)
gloss.w.kop: the header (the short end of a brick)
gloss.w.strek: the stretcher (the long side of a brick)
gloss.s.wall.2: The corner profile must stand straight.
gloss.s.wall.3: Lay the brick with the long side facing out.
gloss.c.wall.q: How high must this row be?
gloss.c.wall: The line keeps the wall straight
gloss.c.wall.b: A bricklayer does not build by eye. First the corner profiles stand straight at both ends of the wall. Between them you pull the brick line tight, at the height of the next row. Lay every brick along the line, but do not push the line away. The gauge rod shows how high each row must be. Check often with the spirit level. A crooked brick is easy to fix while the mortar is wet, and very hard to fix tomorrow.
gloss.c.wall.s: The brick line is loose and hangs a little in the middle. What do you do?
gloss.c.wall.o1: Pull it tight first, then go on.
gloss.c.wall.o2: Lay the bricks under it anyway.
gloss.c.wall.w: A loose line hangs in the middle, so the row hangs too. A tight line gives a straight row.
gloss.w.kapzaag: the tenon saw (a small saw with a stiff back)
gloss.s.wood.3: Hit the chisel with the mallet.
gloss.c.wood.a: The tenon saw, for this small piece.
gloss.c.wood.b: Wood that is sawn too short cannot be made long again. So measure twice, and draw the line before you saw. Saw next to the line, on the side of the piece you do not need. Hold the wood still: on a workbench or with a clamp, not on your knee. Let the saw do the work, with long, calm strokes. Push a chisel away from your body and your other hand. And keep the chisel and the plane sharp: a blunt tool slips more easily.
gloss.c.wood.p: I measure it one more time.
gloss.c.wood.s: You must saw a plank to size. You measured it once, quickly. What do you do?
gloss.c.wood.o1: Measure again, then draw the line.
gloss.c.wood.o2: Saw it now: it is probably right.
gloss.c.wood.o3: Saw it by eye, without a line.
gloss.c.wood.w: Too long you can saw again, too short you cannot fix. Measuring again takes a minute; a new plank takes much more.
gloss.w.winkelhaak: the try square (shows a right angle)
gloss.w.zwaaihaak: the sliding bevel (you set the angle yourself)
gloss.w.kruishout: the marking gauge (draws a line along the edge)
gloss.w.aftekenen: to mark out (draw where you will cut)
gloss.s.square.1: Mark the line with the try square.
gloss.s.square.2: Set the sliding bevel to the right angle.
gloss.s.square.3: Draw a circle with the compasses.
gloss.c.square.a: Yes, the try square fits exactly.
gloss.c.square.b: Before you saw or drill, you mark out where. Use a sharp pencil: a thick line is not exact. Choose one straight edge of the wood, and measure everything from that edge. Hold the thick part of the try square tight against it, and draw the line along the steel. Draw a small cross on the piece you will not use. Then you saw next to the line, on the side of the cross.
gloss.c.square.s: Your pencil is blunt and makes a thick line. You want to mark a plank. What do you do?
gloss.c.square.o1: Sharpen the pencil first, then draw.
gloss.c.square.o2: Draw the line anyway, it is fine.
gloss.c.square.w: A thick line is a few millimetres wide. Then you do not know where to saw, and the piece is not exact.
gloss.s.screw.1: Drill a hole and put a wall plug in it.
gloss.s.screw.2: Which bit goes with this screw?
gloss.s.screw.3: Hammer the nail into the wood.
gloss.c.screw.a: On the charger, it is almost full.
gloss.c.screw.b: Before you drill in a wall, think about what is behind it. Pipes and cables often run straight up, down or across from a socket or a switch. Ask where they are, or check with a detector. Choose a drill the same size as the wall plug, and drill the hole a little deeper than the plug. Use the right bit for the screw: a wrong bit slips and ruins the head of the screw. Wear safety glasses when you drill.
gloss.c.screw.s: You must drill a hole right above a socket. What do you do?
gloss.c.screw.o1: Ask first where the cable runs.
gloss.c.screw.o2: Drill: there is never a cable.
gloss.c.screw.o3: Drill slowly, then it is safe.
gloss.c.screw.w: A cable often runs straight up from a socket. Drilling into it is dangerous, and the repair is a lot of work.
gloss.w.bevestigen: to fix (attach something firmly to a wall)
gloss.w.vastzetten: to tighten (turn until it is tight)
gloss.s.fix.1: Fix the shelf to the wall.
gloss.s.fix.2: Tighten the bolt with the Allen key.
gloss.s.fix.3: Take the flat screwdriver, not the cross one.
gloss.c.fix.q: How do I fix this shelf?
gloss.c.fix.a: With two wall plugs and two screws.
gloss.c.fix.b: A screw or a bolt must be tight, but not too tight. Turn too hard, and the thread breaks or the wood splits. Turn until it does not move any more, then stop. On a cordless drill, first turn the ring with the numbers to a low number. A shelf on the wall needs plugs that fit the wall: stone needs other plugs than a thin board wall. Glue needs time: press the parts together, hold them with a clamp, and wait until the glue is dry.
gloss.c.fix.s: You glued two pieces of wood. Your colleague wants to use it right away. What do you do?
gloss.c.fix.o1: Say: the glue must dry first.
gloss.c.fix.o2: Let them use it: glue is fast.
gloss.c.fix.o3: Hold it in your hands for a minute.
gloss.c.fix.w: Wet glue does not hold yet. Use it too early, and the parts come loose again. Then you must start again.
gloss.w.balk: the block, the cuboid (a long box shape)
gloss.s.shapes.3: A brick has the shape of a cuboid.
gloss.c.shapes.a: No, a rectangle. It is longer than it is wide.
gloss.c.shapes: Check a rectangle with two lines across
gloss.c.shapes.b: A room, a floor or a frame is often a rectangle. But are the corners really square? There is an easy check. Measure from one corner to the corner across. Then measure between the other two corners. Are the two lengths the same? Then the corners are right. Not the same? Then the shape leans a little, and tiles or a floor will not fit well. Tell your supervisor before you start.
gloss.c.shapes.p: These two measurements are not the same.
gloss.c.shapes.s: You measure a floor from corner to corner, both ways. One is longer. What do you do?
gloss.c.shapes.o1: Tell your supervisor before you start.
gloss.c.shapes.o2: Start in a corner, it will be fine.
gloss.c.shapes.w: Two different lengths mean the corners are not square. Then tiles or planks do not fit. It is better to know that before you start.
gloss.w.geodriehoek: the set square with a protractor
gloss.s.angles.2: Measure the angle with the set square.
gloss.s.angles.3: The pipe has the shape of a cylinder.
gloss.c.angles.q: How many degrees is this angle?
gloss.c.angles: Check a big corner with 3, 4 and 5
gloss.c.angles.b: On a building site you often check a right angle: a wall on a floor, a corner of a room. A small corner you check with a try square or a set square. For a big corner there is an old trick. Measure 3 metres along one side and 4 metres along the other side, and make a mark at both. Is it exactly 5 metres from mark to mark? Then the angle is 90 degrees. Smaller works too: 30, 40 and 50 centimetres.
gloss.c.angles.s: You must check a big corner of a new wall. Your square is much too small. What do you do?
gloss.c.angles.o2: Look at it from far away.
gloss.c.angles.w: With 3, 4 and 5 you can check a big corner exactly, with only a tape measure. By eye, a corner can look right and still be wrong.
gloss.w.oppervlakte: the area (length times width, in square metres)
gloss.w.inhoud: the volume (length times width times height)
gloss.s.size.1: The area is the length times the width.
gloss.s.size.2: The volume is length times width times height.
gloss.c.size.q: How many square metres is the floor?
gloss.c.size.a: Four by five metres, so twenty square metres.
gloss.c.size: Work out what you need, then add a little
gloss.c.size.b: How many tiles, how much paint, how much sand? You work it out with the area or the volume. Area: the length times the width, in square metres. Volume: the length times the width times the height, in cubic metres. Measure everything in the same unit: all in metres, or all in centimetres. Write the measurements down, do not keep them in your head. Then add a little extra, for the cut pieces and for mistakes. Not sure? Ask a colleague to check your sum.
gloss.c.size.s: You measured the floor. You must order the tiles today. What do you do?
gloss.c.size.o1: Work out the area, and add a little.
gloss.c.size.o2: Order the area, not one tile more.
gloss.c.size.o3: Guess: you have seen the floor.
gloss.c.size.w: You always cut some tiles, and some break. With a little extra, you do not have to stop halfway and order again.
gloss.w.bedieningspaneel: the control panel (the buttons and screen of a machine)
gloss.w.afscherming: the machine guard (a cover over the moving parts)
gloss.w.sensor: the sensor (it sees if something is there)
gloss.w.signaallamp: the signal light (coloured lights on top of a machine)
gloss.s.atmachine.2: The signal light is red. There is a fault.
gloss.s.atmachine.3: Never take the machine guard away.
gloss.c.atmachine.q: Why does the machine keep stopping?
gloss.c.atmachine.a: The sensor does not see the box well.
gloss.c.atmachine.b: The moving parts of a machine can pull in a hand, a sleeve or hair in less than a second. The guard is there for that. Never take it away, and never reach behind it while the machine runs. Does a guard or a sensor not work? Then the machine is not safe: stop it and tell your team leader. Is something stuck? First stop the machine, and make sure nobody can start it while you work. How that is done differs per company: ask for the explanation before you start. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.atmachine.s: A box is stuck in the machine, right behind the guard. The machine runs. What do you do?
gloss.c.atmachine.o1: Stop the machine first, then get help.
gloss.c.atmachine.o2: Reach in quickly and pull the box out.
gloss.c.atmachine.o3: Open the guard while it runs.
gloss.c.atmachine.w: A running machine can pull your hand in before you can react. Stopping it takes a moment; a hurt hand takes months.
gloss.w.meetklok: the dial gauge (measures very small differences)
gloss.w.monster: the sample (one product you take out to check)
gloss.w.afkeurbak: the reject bin (for products that are not good)
gloss.s.inspect.1: Put the product on the scales.
gloss.s.inspect.2: This product is damaged. It goes in the reject bin.
gloss.s.inspect.3: I look at the label with the magnifying glass.
gloss.c.inspect.q: How often do I take a sample?
gloss.c.inspect.a: One every hour. Write it on the list.
gloss.c.inspect.b: In a factory you check the products during the work: you weigh them, you measure them, or you look at them closely. Write every check on the list right away, with the time. Not later, from memory. Is one product not right? Put it in the reject bin and look carefully at the next ones. Are more products wrong? Then something is wrong with the machine. Tell your team leader right away. A problem that is found early saves a lot of products. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.inspect.s: The scales show that three products in a row are too light. What do you do?
gloss.c.inspect.o1: Tell your team leader right away.
gloss.c.inspect.o2: Put them back on the line.
gloss.c.inspect.w: Three wrong products in a row point to a problem in the machine. The sooner you tell, the fewer products go to waste.
gloss.w.krimpfolie: the shrink wrap (plastic film that gets tight with heat)
gloss.w.sealmachine: the sealing machine (closes a pack with heat)
gloss.w.vulmateriaal: the filling material (air cushions or paper in a box)
gloss.s.packing.1: Put filling material in the box.
gloss.s.packing.2: Close the box with the tape gun.
gloss.s.packing.3: The sealing machine is hot. Watch out!
gloss.c.packing.q: How many products go in a box?
gloss.c.packing.a: Twelve. It says so on the list.
gloss.c.packing.b: Packing is fast work, and a snap-off knife is very sharp. Always cut away from your body and away from your other hand. Push the blade back in after every cut, also when you put the knife down for a moment. Snap off a blunt piece carefully, and throw it in the box for old blades, not in the normal bin. The sealing machine and the heat gun for shrink wrap get very hot: do not touch the hot parts. And check every box: the right product, the right number, and the label straight. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.packing.p: I push the knife back in first.
gloss.c.packing.s: You put the snap-off knife on the table for a moment. The blade is still out. What do you do?
gloss.c.packing.o1: Push the blade back in first.
gloss.c.packing.o2: Leave it: you need it again soon.
gloss.c.packing.o3: Put it in your pocket like this.
gloss.c.packing.w: An open blade on a table or in a pocket can cut you or a colleague. Pushing it back takes one second.
gloss.w.lekbak: the drip tray (it catches leaking oil)
gloss.s.upkeep.1: Oil is leaking. Put the drip tray under it.
gloss.s.upkeep.2: Wipe the oil away with a cleaning rag.
gloss.s.upkeep.3: Never point the air blow gun at someone.
gloss.c.upkeep.q: When do we grease the machine?
gloss.c.upkeep.a: Every Monday, before the first shift.
gloss.c.upkeep: A clean machine shows its problems
gloss.c.upkeep.b: Small maintenance is often part of the work: wiping, oiling and greasing. Only do it when the machine is off, and when you have learned how. A clean machine is easy to check: you see a leak or a loose part right away. Oil on the floor is slippery. Put a drip tray under a leak, wipe the floor, and tell your team leader. Throw oily rags in the special bin. Never point an air blow gun at a person, and never clean your clothes or skin with it. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.upkeep.s: You see a small pool of oil under the machine. What do you do?
gloss.c.upkeep.o1: Put a drip tray under it, and report it.
gloss.c.upkeep.o2: Leave it: it is only a little.
gloss.c.upkeep.o3: Put some paper on it, and go on.
gloss.c.upkeep.w: A leak gets bigger, and oil on the floor makes people slip. Found early, it is a small repair.
gloss.w.draad: the wire (one wire, inside a cable)
gloss.w.kabelgoot: the cable duct (a channel for cables)
gloss.s.wiring.1: Strip one centimetre off the wire.
gloss.s.wiring.2: Fix the wires in the lever connector.
gloss.s.wiring.3: The cables go in the cable duct.
gloss.c.wiring.a: Brown to brown, blue to blue.
gloss.c.wiring: Colours tell what a wire does
gloss.c.wiring.b: In a building the wires have fixed colours. Brown (sometimes black or grey) brings the power. Blue goes back. Green and yellow is the earth: it protects people, and it is never used for anything else. Connect the same colour to the same colour. Strip only as much as fits in the connector: no bare copper may stick out. Push the wire in, then pull it softly to check that it is fixed. Not sure which wire is which? Stop and ask.
gloss.c.wiring.s: You connect a lamp. A piece of copper sticks out of the connector. What do you do?
gloss.c.wiring.o1: Cut it shorter, and connect again.
gloss.c.wiring.o3: Put a piece of tape around it.
gloss.c.wiring.w: Bare copper outside the connector can touch something. That can give a shock or a short circuit, also months later.
gloss.w.spanningzoeker: the voltage tester (a screwdriver with a small lamp)
gloss.w.zekering: the circuit breaker (it switches off the power when something is wrong)
gloss.s.testing.2: Put a padlock on the switch.
gloss.c.testing.q: May I open the fuse box?
gloss.c.testing.b: Before you work on electrics, take three steps. Switch it off: the right circuit breaker in the fuse box, not only the switch on the wall. Lock it: put your own padlock on it and keep the key with you, so nobody can switch it on again. Measure: check with a voltage tester or a multimeter that there is really no power. Only then you start. Does a breaker trip again and again? Do not keep switching it on: tell your supervisor. Only do electrical work when you have been told that you may. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.testing.p: There is no power on it any more.
gloss.c.testing.s: You switched off the breaker. A colleague says: "Start now, it is off." What do you do?
gloss.c.testing.o3: Touch the wire quickly to check.
gloss.c.testing.w: Sometimes the wrong breaker is off, or someone switches it on again. A lock and a measurement show that it is really safe.
gloss.w.afsluiter: the stopcock (it shuts off the water)
gloss.w.teflontape: the thread tape (white tape for the thread of a pipe)
gloss.s.pipes.2: Cut the pipe with the pipe cutter.
gloss.s.pipes.3: Wrap thread tape around the thread.
gloss.c.pipes.a: A little. I will tighten it a bit more.
gloss.c.pipes: Water off first, and a bucket ready
gloss.c.pipes.b: Before you open a water pipe, close the stopcock. Then open a tap lower down, so the pipe gets empty. Put a bucket and a cloth under the place where you work. Cut a copper pipe with a pipe cutter, not with a saw: the end stays round and clean. Tighten a fitting firmly, but not too hard. When you are finished, open the water slowly and look for drops. A small leak that you leave becomes water damage.
gloss.c.pipes.s: You made a new fitting. You open the water. One small drop falls every minute. What do you do?
gloss.c.pipes.o1: Close the water, and tighten or redo it.
gloss.c.pipes.o2: Leave it: it is only one drop.
gloss.c.pipes.o3: Put a bucket under it and go home.
gloss.c.pipes.w: One drop a minute is many litres a week. The water can damage the floor or the ceiling below.
gloss.w.bankschroef: the vice (it holds a part tight on the workbench)
gloss.w.vijl: the file (to make metal smooth by hand)
gloss.w.kolomboormachine: the pillar drill (a big drill on a stand)
gloss.w.draadtap: the tap (it cuts a thread in a hole)
gloss.w.braam: the burr (a sharp edge after cutting metal)
gloss.s.metalwork.1: Clamp the metal in the vice.
gloss.s.metalwork.3: Keep your hands away from the drill.
gloss.c.metalwork.q: Why is the edge so sharp?
gloss.c.metalwork.a: There is still a burr on it.
gloss.c.metalwork.b: At the pillar drill, never hold a small part in your hand. The drill can grab it and turn it round very fast. Clamp it in the vice. Tie long hair back, and wear no gloves at a turning drill: it can pull a glove in. Wear safety glasses. After sawing or drilling, metal has a burr: a sharp edge. File it off before you take the part in your hand or pass it on. Sweep metal chips away with a brush, not with your hand.
gloss.c.metalwork.s: You must drill a hole in a small piece of metal. The vice is on another bench. What do you do?
gloss.c.metalwork.o1: Get the vice, and clamp the piece.
gloss.c.metalwork.o2: Hold it tight with your hand.
gloss.c.metalwork.o3: Put on gloves and hold it.
gloss.c.metalwork.w: A drill can grab a small part and spin it round. Then it hits your hand. In the vice it stays still.
gloss.w.werkinstructie: the work instruction (a sheet with the steps)
gloss.w.mal: the jig (it holds the part in the right place)
gloss.w.voetpedaal: the foot pedal (a switch you press with your foot)
gloss.s.assembly.2: The parts bin is almost empty.
gloss.s.assembly.3: Put the part in the jig.
gloss.c.assembly.a: Step four. Look at the work instruction.
gloss.c.assembly: Follow the steps, in the same order
gloss.c.assembly.b: At an assembly line every step has its place and its order. The work instruction shows them, often with pictures. Do the steps in the same order every time, also when you think you know a faster way. Another order can make a product that looks good but does not work. Is a bin almost empty? Say it in time, so the line does not stop. Do you see a step that could be better? Tell your team leader: then it can change for everyone.
gloss.c.assembly.s: You found a faster way to do step three. The work instruction says something else. What do you do?
gloss.c.assembly.o2: Do it your way from now on.
gloss.c.assembly.w: The order is often there for a reason you cannot see. If your way is better, it can change for everyone.
gloss.w.schroefmachine: the power screwdriver (it hangs above the line)
gloss.w.momentsleutel: the torque wrench (it clicks when the bolt is tight enough)
gloss.s.fastening.1: Tighten the bolt with the torque wrench.
gloss.s.fastening.3: Tie the cables together with a cable tie.
gloss.c.fastening.q: How tight must this bolt be?
gloss.c.fastening.b: A torque wrench clicks when a bolt is tight enough. Stop at the click: do not turn further. Too tight can break the bolt or the part, and too loose can come off. The power screwdriver works the same way: it stops by itself. Put every washer in its place: a missing washer is hard to see later. Count your bolts. Is one left over, or do you need one more? Then something is wrong: tell your team leader.
gloss.c.fastening.p: There is a bolt left over.
gloss.c.fastening.s: Your torque wrench clicked. The bolt still feels a little loose to you. What do you do?
gloss.c.fastening.o1: Stop, and ask your team leader.
gloss.c.fastening.o2: Turn it a bit more by hand.
gloss.c.fastening.w: The click is set to the right force. If it feels wrong, the wrench may need a check. Turning further can break the bolt.
gloss.w.takel: the hoist (it lifts heavy parts with a chain)
gloss.w.tilhulp: the lifting aid (it holds a part with suction)
gloss.w.draaitafel: the turntable (you turn the part, not yourself)
gloss.w.rolcontainer: the roll cage (a tall cage on wheels)
gloss.s.handling.1: Do not lift this alone. Use the hoist.
gloss.s.handling.2: Is the lifting hook closed properly?
gloss.s.handling.3: Push the parts trolley, do not pull it.
gloss.c.handling.q: May I stand under the hoist?
gloss.c.handling.a: No, never under a hanging load.
gloss.c.handling: Let the hoist do the heavy work
gloss.c.handling.b: Heavy parts are lifted with a hoist or a lifting aid, not with your back. Check the hook before you lift: the latch must close. Lift slowly, and keep your hands and feet away from the load. Never stand or walk under a hanging load. Use the turntable to turn a part: then you do not have to twist your back. Push a trolley or a roll cage: you see where you go, and your back has less work. Only use a hoist when you have learned how. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.handling.s: A part is very heavy. The hoist is busy for ten more minutes. What do you do?
gloss.c.handling.w: A heavy part can hurt your back in one second. Ten minutes of waiting is better than months of pain.
gloss.w.typeplaatje: the rating plate (a small metal plate with the type and number)
gloss.w.goedkeursticker: the OK sticker (a green sticker: the product is good)
gloss.s.finalcheck.2: There is a scratch on this product.
gloss.s.finalcheck.3: Without the OK sticker it does not leave.
gloss.c.finalcheck.a: No, there is a crack in it.
gloss.c.finalcheck: Only good products get the sticker
gloss.c.finalcheck.b: The final check is the last chance to find a mistake before the customer finds it. Check every point on the list, also when it is busy. A small scratch or crack is easy to miss: look in good light, and from more than one side. Only put the OK sticker or the stamp on it when every point is good. Not sure? Put the product aside and ask. A mistake that is found here costs little, and a mistake at the customer costs a lot. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.finalcheck.s: The line is busy. You see a small scratch on a product, under the label. What do you do?
gloss.c.finalcheck.o1: Put it aside, and tell your team leader.
gloss.c.finalcheck.o2: Put the sticker on: it is small.
gloss.c.finalcheck.o3: Move the label over the scratch.
gloss.c.finalcheck.w: A small scratch can be a sign of a problem in the line. Hiding it only moves the problem to the customer.
gloss.w.stek: the cutting (a piece of a plant that grows new roots)
gloss.s.sowing.1: Put two seeds in each cell.
gloss.s.sowing.2: Put the cutting in the potting soil.
gloss.s.sowing.3: Give the young plants a little water.
gloss.c.sowing.q: How deep must the seed go?
gloss.c.sowing: Small plants need a gentle hand
gloss.c.sowing.b: Young plants are weak. Hold a cutting or a seedling by a leaf, not by the stem: a leaf grows again, a broken stem does not. Press the soil softly, not hard. Give water slowly, with a fine spray, so the seeds do not wash away. Work with clean hands and clean trays: young plants get sick easily. Write the date and the kind of plant on every tray, so everyone knows what is in it.
gloss.c.sowing.p: I hold it by the leaf.
gloss.c.sowing.s: You must move a small seedling to a pot. What do you do?
gloss.c.sowing.o1: Hold it gently by a leaf.
gloss.c.sowing.o2: Pull it up by the stem.
gloss.c.sowing.o3: Squeeze it out with the soil.
gloss.c.sowing.w: A leaf can grow again. A broken stem cannot, and then the plant dies.
gloss.w.tros: the truss (a bunch of tomatoes on one stem)
gloss.w.bakje: the punnet (a small box for fruit)
gloss.w.kleurenkaart: the colour chart (it shows how ripe the fruit must be)
gloss.s.sorting.1: Put the trusses carefully in the crate.
gloss.s.sorting.2: This tomato is too ripe. It goes aside.
gloss.c.sorting.a: No, still too green. Leave it on the plant.
gloss.c.sorting.b: Fruit and vegetables bruise easily. Put them down, do not drop or throw them. You do not see a bruise today, but tomorrow the fruit is soft and brown. Look at the colour chart to know which colour goes where. Put a damaged or rotten fruit aside: one bad fruit in a punnet can spoil the others. Keep the punnets and crates clean, and never put them on the floor.
gloss.c.sorting.s: You are packing punnets. One tomato has a soft brown spot. What do you do?
gloss.c.sorting.w: A rotten tomato makes the others rot faster. The customer finds it, and the whole punnet comes back.
gloss.w.buisrailkar: the pipe-rail trolley (it rides on the heating pipes)
gloss.w.druppelaar: the dripper (it gives water drop by drop)
gloss.w.luchtraam: the roof vent (a window in the roof)
gloss.w.kasscherm: the greenhouse screen (a cloth under the roof)
gloss.s.greenhouse.1: Ride the pipe-rail trolley to the end of the row.
gloss.s.greenhouse.3: It is warm. The roof vents are opening.
gloss.c.greenhouse.q: Why is it so warm in the greenhouse?
gloss.c.greenhouse.a: The screen is closed, and the vents too.
gloss.c.greenhouse: Leave the climate to the computer
gloss.c.greenhouse.b: In a greenhouse a computer sets the climate: the vents, the screen, the heating and the water. Do not open a vent or change a setting yourself. Do you see something strange, like a dripper that leaks or a vent that does not close? Tell your supervisor. The pipe-rail trolley rides on the heating pipes: only use it when you have learned how. Keep your feet on the platform, and never touch the pipes: they can be hot. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.greenhouse.s: A dripper is loose. Water runs onto the floor. What do you do?
gloss.c.greenhouse.o1: Put it back, and tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.greenhouse.o2: Leave it: it is only water.
gloss.c.greenhouse.o3: Turn off the water for the whole row.
gloss.c.greenhouse.w: A loose dripper wastes water, the plant gets too little, and a wet floor is slippery.
gloss.w.luis: the aphid (a small green insect on plants)
gloss.w.vangplaat: the sticky trap (a yellow card that catches insects)
gloss.w.sluipwesp: the parasitic wasp (a small wasp that kills pests)
gloss.w.ontsmettingsmat: the disinfection mat (you step on it at the door)
gloss.s.pests.1: There are aphids on this leaf.
gloss.s.pests.2: Hang the sticky trap above the plants.
gloss.c.pests.a: No, that is a parasitic wasp. It helps us.
gloss.c.pests: Do not carry diseases from row to row
gloss.c.pests.b: A disease or a pest spreads fast in a greenhouse. You can carry it on your hands, your clothes and your tools. So walk over the disinfection mat at every door, and wash your hands when you go to another part of the greenhouse. Start your work in the healthy rows, and end in the sick rows. Do you see insects, spots or mould on a plant? Do not touch it, but tell your supervisor where it is. Some insects in the greenhouse are helpers: leave them alone. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.pests.s: You see grey mould on a few plants in your row. What do you do?
gloss.c.pests.o1: Tell your supervisor where it is.
gloss.c.pests.o2: Pick off the bad leaves and go on.
gloss.c.pests.o3: Say nothing: it is only a few plants.
gloss.c.pests.w: Mould spreads fast. Your supervisor knows what to do, and where to start.
gloss.w.bandenprofiel: the tyre tread (the grooves in the tyre)
gloss.w.bandenwisselaar: the tyre changer (a machine to take a tyre off the rim)
gloss.s.tyres.2: The tyre tread is too low.
gloss.s.tyres.3: Measure the pressure with the tyre pressure gauge.
gloss.c.tyres.a: Yes, the tread is almost gone.
gloss.c.tyres: Turn in by hand, tighten with the torque wrench
gloss.c.tyres.b: An impact wrench is fast and very strong. Use it to take wheel bolts off, but not to tighten them hard. First turn the bolts in by hand. Then tighten them crosswise with a torque wrench, to the force for that car. A wheel that is not tight can come off while driving. Check the tread and the pressure of every tyre that you take in your hands. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.tyres.p: I turn them in by hand first.
gloss.c.tyres.s: You put a wheel back. A colleague says: "Use the impact wrench, it is faster." What do you do?
gloss.c.tyres.o1: Turn them in by hand, then use the torque wrench.
gloss.c.tyres.o2: Tighten them hard with the impact wrench.
gloss.c.tyres.o3: Turn them in by hand, and leave it.
gloss.c.tyres.w: An impact wrench can make a bolt too tight or not tight enough. Only the torque wrench gives the right force.
gloss.w.oliepeilstok: the dipstick (it shows how much oil there is)
gloss.w.opvangbak: the drain pan (it catches the old oil)
gloss.s.oilchange.1: Put the drain pan under the engine.
gloss.c.oilchange.q: How much oil must go in?
