gloss.c.oilchange.a: Four litres. Then look at the dipstick.
gloss.c.oilchange: Old oil goes in the drum, not in the drain
gloss.c.oilchange.b: Old oil is bad for water and soil. A little oil can make a lot of water dirty. So catch all the old oil in the drain pan, and pour it into the drum for old oil. Never pour it into a drain or a sink. Old filters and oily cloths go into their own bin. Hot oil can burn your skin: let the engine cool down a little first, and wear gloves. Clean up spilled oil right away: oil on the floor is slippery. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.oilchange.p: Where does the old oil go?
gloss.c.oilchange.s: The drain pan is full of old oil. The drum is at the other end of the workshop. What do you do?
gloss.c.oilchange.o1: Carry it to the drum, carefully.
gloss.c.oilchange.o2: Pour it into the drain outside.
gloss.c.oilchange.o3: Leave it under the car for later.
gloss.c.oilchange.w: Old oil in a drain makes the water dirty. A full pan under a car gets kicked over.
gloss.s.brakes.3: The left rear light does not work.
gloss.c.brakes.q: Does the brake disc need replacing too?
gloss.c.brakes.b: Brakes keep people alive. So work calmly, and check your work twice. After new pads or discs, press the brake pedal a few times before the car moves: the first press often goes too deep. Brake fluid is bad for your skin and for paint: wear gloves, and wipe up drops right away. Do not blow brake dust away with compressed air: clean it with brake cleaner and a cloth. Before the car leaves, check every light, also the brake lights.
gloss.c.brakes.p: I press the brake pedal a few times.
gloss.c.brakes.s: You fitted new brake pads. The car must go outside. What do you do?
gloss.c.brakes.o1: Press the brake pedal a few times.
gloss.c.brakes.w: After new pads the pedal can go too deep the first time. Then the car does not stop.
gloss.l.diagnosis: Reading faults and the job card
gloss.w.diagnosecomputer: the diagnostic tester (it reads the faults of the car)
gloss.w.werkorder: the job card (what must be done on the car)
gloss.w.stoelhoes: the seat cover (it keeps the seat clean)
gloss.s.diagnosis.3: Put a seat cover on the seat.
gloss.c.diagnosis.q: What must be done on this car?
gloss.c.diagnosis: Treat the car as if it is your own
gloss.c.diagnosis.b: A customer gives you their car and their key. Treat both with care. Put a seat cover on the seat and a mat on the floor before you get in. Do only what is on the job card. Do you find something else that is wrong? Write it down and tell your supervisor: the customer decides. Keep the key in its place, with its label. Do not use the radio, the phone or the things in the car. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.diagnosis.p: This is not on the job card.
gloss.c.diagnosis.s: You change the oil. A tyre is almost bald. It is not on the job card. What do you do?
gloss.c.diagnosis.o1: Write it down, and tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.diagnosis.o3: Say nothing: it is not your job.
gloss.c.diagnosis.w: The customer decides what is done and paid. But they must know that the tyre is dangerous.
gloss.w.zitmaaier: the ride-on mower (a mower you sit on)
gloss.w.bosmaaier: the brush cutter (a mower on a long stick)
gloss.s.mowing.1: First mow the grass along the edge.
gloss.s.mowing.2: The grass is too wet. We will mow tomorrow.
gloss.c.mowing.q: May I take the ride-on mower?
gloss.c.mowing.a: Yes, but first take the stones away.
gloss.c.mowing.b: A mower or a brush cutter can throw a stone very far and very hard. So walk over the grass first, and take away stones, glass and branches. Wear your face shield or safety glasses, ear protection and safety shoes. Keep other people far away. Does someone come close? Stop the machine. Never put your hand under a mower while the engine runs: turn it off, and wait until the blade stands still. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.mowing.p: Would you keep your distance, please?
gloss.c.mowing.s: You are using the brush cutter. A man with a dog walks towards you. What do you do?
gloss.c.mowing.o1: Stop the machine until he has passed.
gloss.c.mowing.o2: Go on: he can see you.
gloss.c.mowing.o3: Turn away from him, and go on.
gloss.c.mowing.w: A stone from a brush cutter can hurt someone badly, also from far away.
gloss.w.snoeien: to prune (to cut branches off a plant)
gloss.s.pruning.1: Prune the bushes along the path.
gloss.s.pruning.2: This branch is dead. Saw it off.
gloss.s.pruning.3: Put the branches on a pile.
gloss.c.pruning.b: Prune with sharp, clean shears. A clean cut heals fast; a torn branch gets sick. Cut just above a bud or a side branch, and do not leave a long piece. Take off the dead and broken branches first. Keep your other hand away from the blades. Wear gloves: some plants have thorns, or make your skin red. Clean the shears after work.
gloss.c.pruning.s: Your pruning shears are blunt. They tear the branches. What do you do?
gloss.c.pruning.o3: Go on: it is only a bush.
gloss.c.pruning.w: Blunt shears tear the branch. The plant gets sick, and you work harder.
gloss.w.heggenschaar: the hedge trimmer (a machine that cuts a hedge)
gloss.w.snoeiafval: the green waste (cut branches and leaves)
gloss.s.hedge.1: Put the tarp under the hedge.
gloss.s.hedge.2: Cut the hedge nice and straight.
gloss.s.hedge.3: Take the green waste away with the wheelbarrow.
gloss.c.hedge.q: How high must the hedge stay?
gloss.c.hedge.a: Up to the line. Not lower.
gloss.c.hedge.b: In spring and summer, birds make nests in hedges and bushes. Nests that birds use are protected. So look into the hedge before you cut. Do you see a nest with eggs or young birds? Do not cut there, and tell your supervisor. Hold the hedge trimmer with both hands. Stand firmly on the ground or on a good ladder, never on a chair or a bucket. Keep the cable behind you.
gloss.c.hedge.s: You are trimming a hedge in May. You see a nest with young birds. What do you do?
gloss.c.hedge.o1: Stop there, and tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.hedge.o3: Take the nest out, and go on.
gloss.c.hedge.w: Nests that birds use are protected. Your supervisor decides what happens with this part of the hedge.
gloss.l.chainsaw: The chainsaw and the leaf blower
gloss.w.zaagbroek: the chainsaw trousers (they stop the chain)
gloss.s.chainsaw.2: Blow the leaves onto a pile.
gloss.s.chainsaw.3: Only fill up when the engine is cold.
gloss.c.chainsaw.q: May I work with the chainsaw?
gloss.c.chainsaw.a: Not yet. First you get a course.
gloss.c.chainsaw.b: A chainsaw is one of the most dangerous tools in green work. Only work with it when you have had a course, and your supervisor says you may. Always wear chainsaw trousers, a helmet with a face shield and ear protection, gloves and safety boots. Never work alone with a chainsaw. Hold it with both hands, and never saw above your shoulders. With a leaf blower: never blow towards people, cars or open windows. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.chainsaw.p: I have not had a course for this yet.
gloss.c.chainsaw.s: A colleague says: "Take the chainsaw, it is easy." You never had a course. What do you do?
gloss.c.chainsaw.o1: Say that you had no course yet.
gloss.c.chainsaw.o3: Take it, and watch a video first.
gloss.c.chainsaw.w: A chainsaw can cut your leg in a second. Without training you do not know how it can kick back.
gloss.w.onkruidbrander: the weed burner (it kills weeds with heat)
gloss.s.weeding.1: Pull the weeds out, with the root.
gloss.s.weeding.2: Hoe the flower bed by the entrance.
gloss.s.weeding.3: Careful: the weed burner is hot.
gloss.c.weeding.a: No, that is a plant. Leave it.
gloss.c.weeding.b: A weed grows back when the root stays in the ground. So pull it out with the root, or hoe just under the soil. Work when the soil is a little wet: then the root comes out easily. Do not use sprays against weeds, unless you have learned how and your supervisor says so. A weed burner is very hot: keep it away from dry grass, leaves, hedges, cars and bins. Never put it down while it burns. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.weeding.p: Is this a weed or a plant?
gloss.c.weeding.s: You are using the weed burner. Next to the path is a dry hedge. What do you do?
gloss.c.weeding.o1: Pull the weeds there by hand.
gloss.c.weeding.w: A dry hedge catches fire fast. A fire near houses or cars is very dangerous.
gloss.w.kluit: the root ball (the soil around the roots)
gloss.w.boompaal: the tree stake (a pole that holds a young tree)
gloss.s.planting.1: Dig a planting hole for the tree.
gloss.s.planting.2: Put the tree straight, next to the stake.
gloss.s.planting.3: Give the new plants a lot of water.
gloss.c.planting.a: At the back of the flower bed, by the wall.
gloss.c.planting: Under the ground: cables and pipes
gloss.c.planting.b: Under the grass and the pavement there are often cables and pipes: for power, gas, water and internet. So dig carefully. Do you see a coloured tape or a plastic plate in the ground, or do you hit something hard? Stop digging, and tell your supervisor. Never dig on with force. Lift a heavy tree or a big root ball together, with your knees bent. Give a new plant water on the same day. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.planting.s: You are digging a planting hole. Your shovel hits a red plastic tape. What do you do?
gloss.c.planting.o1: Stop digging, and tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.planting.o2: Dig on carefully, next to the tape.
gloss.c.planting.o3: Pull the tape out, and go on.
gloss.c.planting.w: A tape in the ground warns that a cable or a pipe is under it. A gas pipe or a power cable is very dangerous.
gloss.w.stoep: the pavement (the path next to the road)
gloss.w.pijlwagen: the arrow trailer (a trailer with a big arrow that warns drivers)
gloss.w.berm: the verge (the grass next to the road)
gloss.s.roadside.1: Put on your vest. We are working by the road.
gloss.s.roadside.2: Put the cones behind the van.
gloss.c.roadside.a: No, wait. A truck is coming.
gloss.c.roadside: By the road: be seen, stay behind the cones
gloss.c.roadside.b: Work by the road is dangerous: drivers look at their phone, or drive too fast. So always wear your high-visibility vest, also for a short job. Put the cones and the signs out before you start, and take them in last. Park the van as a shield between you and the traffic. Stay behind the cones. Never step back without looking, and work with your face to the traffic when you can. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.roadside.p: First I put out the cones.
gloss.c.roadside.s: You must cut one small bush by the road. It takes five minutes. What do you do?
gloss.c.roadside.o1: Put on the vest, and put out the cones.
gloss.c.roadside.o2: Do it fast, without the cones.
gloss.c.roadside.o3: Ask a colleague to watch the cars.
gloss.c.roadside.w: An accident takes only one second. Five minutes without cones is five minutes without protection.
gloss.w.grijper: the litter picker (a stick that grabs rubbish)
gloss.s.litter.1: Pick up the litter with the litter picker.
gloss.s.litter.2: Careful, there is broken glass here.
gloss.s.litter.3: Put the rubbish bags by the trailer.
gloss.c.litter.q: When will this tree be pruned?
gloss.c.litter.a: I do not know. Ask the municipality.
gloss.c.litter.b: In parks and bushes you sometimes find a needle from a syringe. Never pick it up with your hand, also not with gloves on. Use the litter picker, and put the needle in a hard box or bottle with a lid, never in a rubbish bag. Tell your supervisor. Did a needle prick you? Wash the wound with a lot of water, and call a doctor right away. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.litter.s: You see a needle in the grass, next to a bench. What do you do?
gloss.c.litter.o1: Pick it up with the litter picker.
gloss.c.litter.o2: Pick it up with your gloves on.
gloss.c.litter.o3: Put it in the rubbish bag.
gloss.c.litter.w: A needle can carry a disease. Gloves do not stop a needle, and a hard box keeps others safe.
gloss.w.intercom: the intercom (you talk to someone at the door)
gloss.w.toestel: the extension (a phone number inside the building)
gloss.s.reception.1: Good morning, can I help you?
gloss.s.reception.3: Please take a seat in the waiting area.
gloss.c.reception.q: I have an appointment with Mrs Jansen.
gloss.c.reception.a: One moment. I will call her.
gloss.c.reception.b: At the front desk you are the first person a visitor meets. Look up, smile and say hello, also when you are busy on the phone. Speak to visitors with "u". Answer the phone with the name of the company and your own name. Do you not know the answer? Say so, and find someone who knows. Never give names, phone numbers or rooms of staff to people you do not know.
gloss.c.reception.p: Good morning, how can I help you?
gloss.c.reception.s: You are on the phone. A visitor comes to the desk and waits. What do you do?
gloss.c.reception.o1: Look up, and show you will come soon.
gloss.c.reception.o2: Finish your call, without looking up.
gloss.c.reception.o3: Put the phone down at once.
gloss.c.reception.w: A visitor who is seen waits calmly. A visitor who is not seen feels unwelcome.
gloss.w.garderobe: the cloakroom (where you hang your coat)
gloss.w.hal: the hall (the big room at the entrance)
gloss.w.begeleiden: to take someone somewhere (to walk with them)
gloss.s.visitors.1: Would you write your name here?
gloss.s.visitors.3: I will take you to the lift.
gloss.c.visitors.q: Where can I leave my coat?
gloss.c.visitors.a: In the cloakroom, next to the lift.
gloss.c.visitors.b: Every visitor writes their name on the list, or signs in on the screen, and gets a visitor pass. Then you know who is in the building. This is important when there is a fire: everyone must get out, and someone checks the list. At the end of the visit, the visitor gives the pass back. Do not let people in behind you that you do not know: ask kindly who they are here for. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.visitors.s: A man walks in behind a colleague. He has no pass. What do you do?
gloss.c.visitors.o1: Ask him kindly who he is here for.
gloss.c.visitors.o2: Let him go: he came in with staff.
gloss.c.visitors.w: In an emergency, you must know who is inside. And not everyone who walks in has a reason to be there.
gloss.w.postvak: the pigeonhole (a box for post, one per person)
gloss.s.mailroom.2: Put the letters in the right pigeonhole.
gloss.c.mailroom.a: For Finance, on the second floor.
gloss.c.mailroom.b: Post and parcels are private. Never open a letter or a parcel for someone else. Check the name and the department on each item, and put it in the right pigeonhole. When a courier brings a parcel, look at it before you sign: is it damaged? Write that down. Is a parcel strange: it smells, it leaks, or it has no sender? Do not open it, and tell your supervisor. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.mailroom.p: The box is wet and broken.
gloss.c.mailroom.s: A courier brings a parcel. One corner is wet and torn. What do you do?
gloss.c.mailroom.o1: Write the damage down before you sign.
gloss.c.mailroom.o3: Open it, to see if all is there.
gloss.c.mailroom.w: After you sign, it looks as if the parcel was fine. Then nobody pays for the damage.
gloss.w.thermoskan: the thermos jug (it keeps coffee hot)
gloss.s.meetingroom.1: Put ten chairs around the table.
gloss.c.meetingroom.q: What time does the meeting start?
gloss.c.meetingroom.a: At ten. Make sure everything is ready.
gloss.c.meetingroom.b: A meeting room must be ready before the first person comes in. Check the chairs, the table, the projector and the cables. Put coffee, tea and water out, with cups and milk. Carry hot drinks carefully, and never over people. After the meeting, clean the table and take everything back. What you hear in a meeting room, you keep to yourself.
gloss.c.meetingroom.s: The meeting starts in five minutes. The projector does not work. What do you do?
gloss.c.meetingroom.o3: Leave a note on the table.
gloss.c.meetingroom.w: Five minutes is still time to fix it or find another room. Later, everyone waits.
gloss.w.melding: the report (you tell that something is wrong)
gloss.s.faults.2: There is a leak in the kitchen.
gloss.c.faults.q: Why is it so cold here?
gloss.c.faults.a: The heating is broken. The technician comes tomorrow.
gloss.c.faults: Report it, do not fix it alone
gloss.c.faults.b: Do you see something broken, like a leak, a lamp that is out or a door that does not close? Report it, also when it is small: in the system or to your supervisor. Say where it is, what you see and since when. Do not repair electricity, gas or heating yourself. Do you smell gas? Do not use a switch or a phone near it, open the windows, get people out, and call for help outside. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.faults.p: I want to report a fault.
gloss.c.faults.s: Water drips from the ceiling in the corridor. What do you do?
gloss.c.faults.o1: Report it, and put a bucket under it.
gloss.c.faults.o2: Wait: maybe it stops by itself.
gloss.c.faults.w: A small leak can become big damage. A bucket keeps the floor dry, so nobody slips.
gloss.w.vervangen: to replace (to put a new one in)
gloss.s.repairs.1: Replace the lamp in the corridor.
gloss.s.repairs.3: Take the stepladder, not a chair.
gloss.c.repairs.a: Yes, the battery is almost empty.
gloss.c.repairs.b: For a lamp or a high shelf, use a stepladder, never a chair, a table or a box. Put it on a flat floor, open it fully, and do not stand on the top step. Switch off the light before you change a lamp, and let an old lamp cool down. Only do the repairs you have learned. Put your tools back in the toolbox when you are done, so nobody trips over them. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.repairs.s: A lamp in the office is broken. The stepladder is on another floor. What do you do?
gloss.c.repairs.w: A chair can roll or tip over. A fall from a chair can hurt you badly.
gloss.w.werkplek: the workplace (the desk where someone works)
gloss.w.plattegrond: the floor plan (a map of the building)
gloss.s.moving.1: Write the room number on every box.
gloss.s.moving.2: Put the boxes on the hand truck.
gloss.c.moving.a: To room twelve. Look at the floor plan.
gloss.c.moving.b: Moving is heavy work. Do not fill a box too full: books and files are heavy. Lift with your knees bent and your back straight, close to your body. Use the hand truck for more boxes, and lift a desk together. Write the new room number on every box, chair and computer. Unplug the cables first. Never put boxes in a corridor or in front of an emergency exit.
gloss.c.moving.p: Can you help me lift this?
gloss.c.moving.s: You must move a heavy desk. Your colleague is on a break. What do you do?
gloss.c.moving.o1: Wait for help, and lift it together.
gloss.c.moving.w: A heavy desk can hurt your back when you lift it alone. Together it is easy and safe.
gloss.w.ronde: the round (a walk past every room)
gloss.w.nachtslot: the deadlock (the extra lock for the night)
gloss.s.closing.1: I am doing the last round of the building.
gloss.s.closing.3: Put the door on the deadlock.
gloss.c.closing.a: No, everyone has gone. I am locking up.
gloss.c.closing.b: At the end of the day you walk the last round. Check that nobody is left inside, that the windows are closed and the lights are out. The emergency exits stay free. Keep the keys with you, never in a drawer. The alarm code is secret: never give it to anyone, also not on the phone. Does the alarm go off? Follow the steps of your company. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.closing.p: I do not pass on the alarm code.
gloss.c.closing.s: Someone calls: "I am from the alarm company. What is your code?" What do you do?
gloss.c.closing.o1: Say no, and tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.closing.o2: Give the code: he sounds kind.
gloss.c.closing.o3: Give only half of the code.
gloss.c.closing.w: A real alarm company does not ask for your code on the phone. A thief might.
gloss.w.surveilleren: to patrol (to walk around and watch)
gloss.w.terrein: the grounds (the land around a building)
gloss.w.inbraak: the break-in (someone gets in to steal)
gloss.w.openstaan: to be open (a door or window that should be closed)
gloss.s.patrol.1: I do a round every two hours.
gloss.s.patrol.2: The gate behind the hall is open.
gloss.c.patrol.q: Did you see anything during your round?
gloss.c.patrol.a: Yes. A window was open by the back door.
gloss.c.patrol: Look and report, do not play the hero
gloss.c.patrol.b: On your round you look: are doors and windows closed, is the fence whole, is there anyone who should not be there? Write down what you see, with the time. Do you see something strange, like a broken window or a person at night? Do not go in alone. Call the control room or the police on the radio or the phone, and wait at a safe place. Your own safety comes first. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.patrol.p: I see someone by the fence.
gloss.c.patrol.s: At night you see a door that is broken open. You hear noise inside. What do you do?
gloss.c.patrol.o1: Stay outside, and call for help.
gloss.c.patrol.o3: Shout inside that you are coming.
gloss.c.patrol.w: A thief inside can be dangerous. The police know what to do; your job is to see and report.
gloss.w.slagboom: the barrier (a bar across the road that goes up)
gloss.w.toegangspas: the access card (a card that opens the door)
gloss.w.legitimatie: the ID (a passport or an ID card)
gloss.w.draaihek: the turnstile (a gate that turns, for one person at a time)
gloss.w.kenteken: the registration number (the letters and numbers of a car)
gloss.s.access.2: Your card does not work. I will make a call.
gloss.c.access.q: May I go in? I forgot my card.
gloss.c.access.a: Sorry, without a card you may not go in.
gloss.c.access.b: At the gate or the desk you check who comes in. Everyone needs a pass, or must be on the list. Be friendly, also when someone is angry or in a hurry. Do not make exceptions because someone says he is the boss: check it. Never lend your own pass to anyone, and never let someone walk in behind you. A pass that is lost must be reported at once. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.access.s: A man in a suit says: "I am the new director. I have no pass yet." What do you do?
gloss.c.access.o1: Check it, before you let him in.
gloss.c.access.o2: Let him in: he looks important.
gloss.c.access.w: Anyone can say he is the director. A quick check keeps the building safe, and a real director will understand.
gloss.w.meldkamer: the control room (where people watch the cameras and take calls)
gloss.w.camerabeelden: the camera footage (what the camera has filmed)
gloss.w.bewegingsmelder: the motion sensor (it sees when something moves)
gloss.s.cameras.1: On camera three I see someone by the fence.
gloss.s.cameras.3: The control room calls the police.
gloss.c.cameras.q: What do you see on the screen?
gloss.c.cameras.a: A man by the fence. I am sending a colleague.
gloss.c.cameras.b: Cameras film people: staff, visitors and people walking by. What you see on the screens is private. Only watch for your work, and never film the screen with your phone. Never send footage to friends or put it online. Is there an incident? Write down the camera and the time, and tell your supervisor. Only your company decides who gets the footage, for example the police. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.cameras.p: I am not allowed to show that.
gloss.c.cameras.s: A colleague asks you to send him a funny clip from the cameras. What do you do?
gloss.c.cameras.o1: Say no: the footage is private.
gloss.c.cameras.o3: Film the screen with your phone.
gloss.c.cameras.w: The people on the footage did not agree to be shared. Sending it can cost you your job.
gloss.w.logboek: the logbook (a book or an app where you write down everything)
gloss.s.report.1: I am writing a report of the incident.
gloss.s.report.3: I cannot hear you well. Say it again.
gloss.c.report.q: What must go in the report?
gloss.c.report.a: What happened, where and at what time.
gloss.c.report.b: Write a report straight after an incident, while you still remember it well. Write what you saw and heard yourself: what happened, where, at what time, and who was there. Write facts, not what you think. On the radio, speak short and clear, and wait until the other person has finished. Say who you are and where you are. A good report helps the police, your company and you.
gloss.c.report.p: I will write it down right away.
gloss.c.report.s: After a busy night you are very tired. There was one small incident. What do you do?
gloss.c.report.o1: Write the report before you go home.
gloss.c.report.o2: Write it tomorrow, after a good sleep.
gloss.c.report.o3: Skip it: it was only small.
gloss.c.report.w: Tomorrow you forget details. A report without a time or a place helps nobody.
gloss.w.brandmelder: the fire alarm button (a red box you press when there is a fire)
gloss.w.branddeur: the fire door (it stops fire and smoke)
gloss.w.brandmeldcentrale: the fire alarm panel (it shows where the alarm is)
gloss.w.ontruimingsplan: the evacuation plan (who does what when everyone must go out)
gloss.s.evacuation.1: There is a fire alarm in hall two.
gloss.s.evacuation.3: I am waiting for the fire brigade at the entrance.
gloss.c.evacuation.a: No, two people on the list are still missing.
gloss.c.evacuation.b: Do you see fire or smoke? Press the fire alarm button, or call 112. Then help people out by the escape routes, never by the lift. Close doors behind you, but do not lock them. Fight a fire only when it is small and you have learned how. Go to the assembly point, and count who is there. Meet the fire brigade at the entrance, and tell them what you know. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.evacuation.p: Everyone outside, to the assembly point.
gloss.c.evacuation.s: The fire alarm goes. A man wants to take the lift. What do you do?
gloss.c.evacuation.o2: Let him: the lift is faster.
gloss.c.evacuation.o3: Go with him in the lift.
gloss.c.evacuation.w: In a fire, the lift can stop or fill with smoke. The stairs are the safe way out.
gloss.w.aed: the AED (a machine that helps a heart that stopped)
gloss.w.reanimeren: to do CPR (to press on the chest to save a life)
gloss.w.bewusteloos: unconscious (the person does not wake up)
gloss.s.firstaid.2: Get the AED from the reception.
gloss.s.firstaid.3: He is not breathing. I am going to do CPR.
gloss.c.firstaid.a: At the entrance, next to the lift.
gloss.c.firstaid: Call 112, start CPR, get the AED
gloss.c.firstaid.b: Someone falls down and does not react? Call 112 at once, or let someone else call. Check if the person breathes normally. If not: start CPR, and let someone get the AED. The AED speaks and tells you what to do; you cannot do it wrong. Keep going until the ambulance takes over. Do you have a first aid course? Tell your colleagues, so they know who to call.
gloss.c.firstaid.s: A man falls in the hall. He does not move and does not breathe. What do you do?
gloss.c.firstaid.o2: Wait to see if he wakes up.
gloss.c.firstaid.o3: Lift him, and put him on a chair.
gloss.c.firstaid.w: When the heart stops, every minute counts. CPR and an AED can save a life before the ambulance comes.
gloss.w.heterdaad: in the act (you see it happen)
gloss.w.aanhouden: to hold someone (until the police come)
gloss.w.detectiepoortje: the security gate (it beeps at the door)
gloss.w.alarmlabel: the security tag (it makes the gate beep)
gloss.s.shoplifting.1: The gate beeps at the exit.
gloss.s.shoplifting.3: I am holding him until the police come.
gloss.c.shoplifting: Shop theft: watch, report, no rough force
gloss.c.shoplifting.b: Did you see someone steal? Stay calm, and call the police at once. Some shops let a guard hold a thief until the police come; others say: only watch, report and remember what the person looks like. Never hit or kick, and never hold someone by the neck. Never search a person, their pockets or their bag: that is for the police. Write down what you saw, and keep the camera footage. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.shoplifting.p: Would you come with me, please?
gloss.c.shoplifting.s: You saw a woman put a bottle in her bag. She walks out. What do you do?
gloss.c.shoplifting.o1: Stop her calmly, and call the police.
gloss.c.shoplifting.o2: Search her bag at the door, quickly.
gloss.c.shoplifting.o3: Push her hard to the ground.
gloss.c.shoplifting.w: Searching a person is for the police, and rough force can hurt someone and get you into trouble.
gloss.w.huisverbod: the ban (you may not come in here any more)
gloss.w.bodycam: the body camera (a small camera on your uniform)
gloss.s.aggression.1: Calm down, sir. I want to help you.
gloss.s.aggression.2: Keep your distance and stay calm.
gloss.s.aggression.3: You are banned. You must leave now.
gloss.c.aggression.q: Why may I not go in?
gloss.c.aggression.b: An angry person calms down faster when you stay calm. Speak slowly and quietly, and call the person "u". Keep an arm’s length or more between you, and keep a way out behind you. Do not touch the person and do not shout back. Does it get dangerous? Step back, and call a colleague or the police. Write it down afterwards. After a bad incident, talk about it with someone. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.aggression.p: Calm down. I want to help you.
gloss.c.aggression.s: A man shouts at you and comes very close. What do you do?
gloss.c.aggression.w: Calm words and space take the heat out. Shouting or pushing makes it worse.
gloss.w.hygienesluis: the hygiene lock (the room where you get clean before you go in)
gloss.w.laarzenwasser: the boot washer (brushes that clean your boots)
gloss.s.hygienelock.1: Wash your hands and disinfect them.
gloss.s.hygienelock.2: Put on your hair net and your beard net.
gloss.c.hygienelock.q: May I keep my watch on?
gloss.c.hygienelock.b: In a food factory, you are the biggest danger for the food: germs come from your hands, hair and clothes. So go through the hygiene lock every time you go in, also after a break or the toilet. Hair net on, beard net if you have a beard, clean work clothes, all jewellery off. Wash your hands with soap, dry them and disinfect them. Are you ill, with diarrhoea or vomiting? Tell your supervisor before you start. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.hygienelock.p: I have diarrhoea. May I work today?
gloss.c.hygienelock.s: You come back from the toilet. Your colleague says: "Skip the lock, we are busy." What do you do?
gloss.c.hygienelock.w: Germs from the toilet can make many customers ill. A few minutes in the lock prevent that.
gloss.w.allergeen: the allergen (food that makes some people very ill)
gloss.w.gluten: the gluten (in wheat, so in bread and cake)
gloss.w.sesam: the sesame (small seeds, for example on bread)
gloss.w.kruisbesmetting: the cross-contamination (something gets into food where it should not be)
gloss.s.allergens.2: Look on the label which allergens are in it.
gloss.s.allergens.3: Clean everything well after the peanuts.
gloss.c.allergens.q: May this tub go with the others?
gloss.c.allergens.a: No, there are nuts in it.
gloss.c.allergens.b: For some people, a tiny bit of nuts, peanut, milk, egg, gluten or sesame can be life-threatening. That is why the label must say exactly what is in a product. Keep allergens apart: their own tubs, tools and colours. After a product with an allergen, the line is cleaned before the next product. Never swap an ingredient, also not when it looks the same. Do you doubt? Ask. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.allergens.s: The almonds are finished. A colleague says: "Use hazelnuts, nobody will notice." What do you do?
gloss.c.allergens.o1: Say no, and tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.allergens.o3: Use them, and change nothing on the label.
gloss.c.allergens.w: The label must say what is inside. A wrong nut can make someone with an allergy very ill.
gloss.l.coldroom: The cold room and the freezer
gloss.w.koelketen: the cold chain (food stays cold all the way)
gloss.w.thermokleding: the thermal clothes (warm clothes for the cold)
gloss.s.coldroom.1: It is minus eighteen degrees in the freezer room.
gloss.s.coldroom.2: Put the meat in the cold room at once.
gloss.s.coldroom.3: Write the temperature on the list.
gloss.c.coldroom.q: Why is the cold room beeping?
gloss.c.coldroom.a: The door is open. Close it quickly.
gloss.c.coldroom: Cold work: dress warm, keep it cold
gloss.c.coldroom.b: Food must stay cold all the way: from the lorry to the cold room to the shop. So put cold products away at once, and keep the doors of the cold room and the freezer closed. Check the temperature and write it down. In the freezer, wear your thermal clothes, gloves and a hat, and take a warm break in time. Make sure you can always open the door from the inside. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.coldroom.p: It is too warm here. The cooling does not work.
gloss.c.coldroom.s: The thermometer of the cold room shows a much higher number than normal. What do you do?
gloss.c.coldroom.o2: Wait: it will cool down again.
gloss.c.coldroom.o3: Write the normal number on the list.
gloss.c.coldroom.w: Too warm means germs grow. Your supervisor decides if the food is still safe.
gloss.l.foreignbody: Glass, metal and plastic in the food
gloss.w.vreemdvoorwerp: the foreign body (something in the food that does not belong there)
gloss.s.foreignbody.1: The metal detector beeps. Stop the line.
gloss.s.foreignbody.2: Glass has broken at line two.
gloss.s.foreignbody.3: Put the product in the reject bin.
gloss.c.foreignbody.q: What do I do with this bit of plastic?
gloss.c.foreignbody.a: Show it to the shift leader.
gloss.c.foreignbody: Something in the food? Stop and report
gloss.c.foreignbody.b: Glass, metal, plastic, a plaster or a hair must never end up in food. Does the metal detector beep, or do you find something strange? Put the product aside, and tell the shift leader. Did glass break? Stop the line near it: the shift leader decides what must be thrown away. Use only blue plasters, so they are easy to see. Never take glass, pens or loose things onto the work floor. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.foreignbody.p: I found something in the product.
gloss.c.foreignbody.s: A glass lamp breaks above the line. The products roll on. What do you do?
gloss.c.foreignbody.o1: Stop the line, and call the shift leader.
gloss.c.foreignbody.o2: Pick out the glass you can see.
gloss.c.foreignbody.o3: Go on: the detector finds glass.
gloss.c.foreignbody.w: A metal detector does not find glass. Small pieces you cannot see can hurt a customer badly.
gloss.w.uitbenen: to bone (to cut the bones out of meat)
gloss.w.fileren: to fillet (to cut fish or meat into flat pieces)
gloss.s.cutting.3: Sharpen your knife before you start.
gloss.c.cutting.q: How much must go in a tub?
gloss.c.cutting.a: Five hundred grams. Look at the scales.
gloss.c.cutting.b: A sharp knife is safer than a blunt one: you need less force, so it slips less. Always wear your cut-resistant glove on the other hand. Cut away from your body. Put a knife down flat on the board, never in a sink or under meat. Do not try to catch a falling knife: step back. Carry a knife with the point down, close to your leg. Even a small cut must be covered and reported.
gloss.c.cutting.s: Your knife slips out of your hand and falls. What do you do?
gloss.c.cutting.o1: Step back, and let it fall.
gloss.c.cutting.w: A falling knife cuts deep when you grab it. On the floor it can do no harm.
gloss.w.lotnummer: the batch number (one number for one batch of products)
gloss.w.schaal: the tray (a flat dish for food)
gloss.w.omdoos: the outer box (the big box around the small packs)
gloss.s.labels.1: Check that the date on the label is right.
gloss.s.labels.2: This pack is not vacuum-packed. Pack it again.
gloss.s.labels.3: Write the batch number on the list.
gloss.c.labels.q: Which date must go on it?
gloss.c.labels.a: In ten days. Look at the list.
gloss.c.labels.b: The label tells the customer what is inside, how much it weighs and until when it is good. A wrong date or a wrong label can make people ill, for example when an allergen is missing. So check the first labels of every new run: the product, the date and the batch number. Is something wrong? Stop, and tell your supervisor. Products with a wrong label are put aside, never sold. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.labels.s: You see that the date on the labels is one week too late. What do you do?
gloss.c.labels.o1: Stop packing, and tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.labels.o2: Go on: one week does not matter.
gloss.c.labels.o3: Change the date with a pen.
gloss.c.labels.w: A wrong date can let people eat food that is no longer safe. Better to stop now than to call it back later.
gloss.w.naspoelen: to rinse (to wash off with clean water)
gloss.s.linecleaning.2: Spray the foam onto the belt.
gloss.s.linecleaning.3: Then rinse everything with clean water.
gloss.c.linecleaning.a: Not yet. I still have to rinse it.
gloss.c.linecleaning.b: Never clean a machine that is running. Turn it off, and make sure nobody can start it again: follow the steps of your company. Wear the right gloves, glasses and boots: cleaning products can burn your skin and eyes. Never mix products. First take away the leftovers, then foam, scrub and rinse. Do not spray water on electric boxes or plugs. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.linecleaning.s: Some meat is stuck in the belt. The machine is still running. What do you do?
gloss.c.linecleaning.o1: Turn it off first, then take it out.
gloss.c.linecleaning.o2: Pull it out quickly with your hand.
gloss.c.linecleaning.o3: Push it out with a knife.
gloss.c.linecleaning.w: A running belt can pull in your hand in a second. Turning it off takes only a moment.
gloss.w.controlepunt: the check point (a step where you must check something)
gloss.w.kerntemperatuur: the core temperature (the temperature inside the food)
gloss.w.prikthermometer: the probe thermometer (you stick it into the food)
gloss.w.afwijking: the deviation (something is not as it should be)
gloss.w.steekproef: the spot check (you test a few products)
gloss.s.haccp.1: Measure the core temperature with the probe thermometer.
gloss.s.haccp.3: Is something wrong? Report it at once.
gloss.c.haccp.q: Why must I write everything down?
gloss.c.haccp.a: That way we know the food is safe.
gloss.c.haccp.b: Every food company works with a food safety plan (HACCP). It says at which steps you must check something, like the temperature of the cold room or the core temperature of cooked meat. You check, you write it down, and you sign. Write what you really measured, also when it is wrong. A wrong number is not your fault, but hiding it is dangerous. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.haccp.s: You forgot to measure at ten. Your colleague says: "Just write down a good number." What do you do?
gloss.c.haccp.o1: Measure now, and write the real time.
gloss.c.haccp.o2: Write a good number for ten o’clock.
gloss.c.haccp.w: The list must show what really happened. A made-up number hides a problem that can make people ill.
gloss.w.vuilniswagen: the bin lorry, the garbage truck
gloss.w.kliko: the wheelie bin (a bin on wheels)
gloss.w.kieplift: the bin lift (it lifts the bin and tips it out)
gloss.w.treeplank: the back step (a step at the back of the lorry)
gloss.w.bijplaatsing: the extra rubbish (bags left next to the bin)
gloss.s.binlorry.1: Put the wheelie bin on the bin lift.
gloss.s.binlorry.2: There are bags next to the container.
gloss.s.binlorry.3: The wheelie bin is too heavy. Leave it.
gloss.c.binlorry.q: May I ride on the back?
gloss.c.binlorry.a: No, you get into the cab.
gloss.c.binlorry.b: Wear your high-visibility clothes on every round. Get in and out on the side of the pavement, never on the side of the traffic. Ride in the cab, not on the back of the lorry: only when your company clearly allows it, and never when it reverses or goes fast. Keep away from the bin lift while it moves. Is a bin too heavy, or does something stick out of it? Leave it, and report it. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.binlorry.p: This wheelie bin is too heavy.
gloss.c.binlorry.s: The next street is very close. The driver says: "Stand on the back step." What do you do?
gloss.c.binlorry.o2: Stand on the step: it is close.
gloss.c.binlorry.w: Falling off a moving lorry is one of the biggest dangers of this work. In the cab you are safe.
gloss.w.dodehoek: the blind spot (where the driver cannot see you)
gloss.w.aanwijzer: the banksman (the person who guides the driver)
gloss.s.reversing.2: I cannot see you in the mirror.
gloss.s.reversing.3: Make eye contact with the driver.
gloss.c.reversing.a: Yes, I am on the left. Look in your mirror.
gloss.c.reversing.b: Many accidents with waste lorries happen when they drive backwards. The driver cannot see right behind the lorry: the blind spot. So never stand or walk behind a lorry that may reverse. Guide the driver from the side, where you can see each other in the mirror. Lost eye contact? The driver stops. Agree on clear signs before you start. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.reversing.p: Stop! I cannot see you any more.
gloss.c.reversing.s: The lorry reverses. You walk behind it to get a bag. What do you do?
gloss.c.reversing.o1: Wait until the lorry stands still.
gloss.c.reversing.o2: Walk fast: it is only a second.
gloss.c.reversing.o3: Wave to the driver, and go.
gloss.c.reversing.w: A driver cannot see you behind the lorry. One second is enough for an accident.
gloss.w.gft: the food and garden waste (fruit, vegetables and plants)
gloss.w.restafval: the general waste (what cannot be sorted)
gloss.s.wastesorting.1: The glass goes in the bottle bank.
gloss.s.wastesorting.2: This belongs with the general waste.
gloss.c.wastesorting.q: Where does a pizza box go?
gloss.c.wastesorting.a: With the general waste. There is grease on it.
gloss.c.wastesorting.b: Sorted waste can be used again: paper becomes paper, glass becomes glass. But one wrong thing can spoil a whole load. So look in the bin before you empty it. Does something not belong there, like a bag of general waste in the paper? Leave it, or follow the rules of your company. Which waste goes where differs per town: learn the rules of your area. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.wastesorting.p: This does not belong in here.
gloss.c.wastesorting.s: A paper bin is full of black rubbish bags. What do you do?
gloss.c.wastesorting.o3: Take the bags out by hand.
gloss.c.wastesorting.w: Rubbish in the paper spoils the whole load. Bags can also hold sharp or dirty things.
gloss.w.snijwond: the cut (a wound from something sharp)
gloss.w.prikken: to prick (a sharp point goes into your skin)
gloss.w.tetanusprik: the tetanus jab (an injection against an illness from dirt in a wound)
gloss.s.wastesafety.1: Never hold a bag from below.
gloss.s.wastesafety.2: Careful, there is glass in this bag.
gloss.s.wastesafety.3: I pricked myself on a needle.
gloss.c.wastesafety.q: I have cut myself. What must I do?
gloss.c.wastesafety.a: Wash the wound well. And tell me.
gloss.c.wastesafety.b: A rubbish bag can hold glass, knives or needles. So never press a bag against your body, never squeeze it, and never carry it on your leg: hold it at the top, away from you. Wear your gloves. Lift with your knees bent and your back straight, and push a bin, do not carry it. Did something prick or cut you? Wash the wound well with water, and tell your supervisor the same day.
gloss.c.wastesafety.s: A bag tears. You see a needle in it. What do you do?
gloss.c.wastesafety.o1: Do not touch it, and report it.
gloss.c.wastesafety.o2: Pick it up with your gloves on.
gloss.c.wastesafety.o3: Push it back in the bag.
gloss.c.wastesafety.w: Gloves do not stop a needle. A needle can carry a disease.
gloss.w.milieustraat: the recycling yard (where people bring big or special waste)
gloss.w.grofvuil: the bulky waste (big things, like a sofa)
gloss.w.weegbrug: the weighbridge (a scale for cars and lorries)
gloss.w.afvalpas: the waste pass (residents show it at the gate)
gloss.s.yard.1: The rubble goes in container four.
gloss.s.yard.2: May I see your waste pass?
gloss.c.yard.a: In the container for bulky waste, at the back.
gloss.c.yard: Help, but keep the yard safe
gloss.c.yard.b: At the recycling yard you tell visitors where their waste goes, and you check that it is sorted well. Be friendly: many people come only a few times a year and do not know the rules. Keep children and visitors away from machines and from the edge of high containers. Lift heavy things together, or let the visitor carry their own. Does someone bring something you do not know? Ask before it goes in. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.yard.s: A man wants to throw a full bag in the wood container. What do you do?
gloss.c.yard.o1: Ask what is in the bag.
gloss.c.yard.o2: Let him: it is his waste.
gloss.c.yard.w: One wrong thing can spoil a full container. A friendly question keeps the waste clean.
gloss.w.chemischafval: the chemical waste (dangerous waste, like paint and oil)
gloss.w.asbest: the asbestos (a dangerous material in old buildings)
gloss.w.gevarensymbool: the hazard symbol (a picture that warns for danger)
gloss.s.hazardous.1: Put the paint with the chemical waste.
gloss.s.hazardous.2: This bottle is leaking. Pick it up with gloves.
gloss.c.hazardous.a: I do not know. Put it aside.
gloss.c.hazardous: Unknown? Do not open, do not smell
gloss.c.hazardous.b: Chemical waste, like paint, oil, cleaning products, batteries and spray cans, can burn, poison or explode. Look for the hazard symbols. Wear gloves and safety glasses. Never open a bottle to smell what is inside, and never mix products. Keep a leaking bottle upright, and put it in a tray. Asbestos may only come in when it is packed well: never break it, and do not take it out of the packing. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.hazardous.s: A woman brings a bottle without a label. It smells strong. What do you do?
gloss.c.hazardous.o1: Put it apart, and tell your supervisor.
gloss.c.hazardous.o2: Open it, and smell what it is.
gloss.c.hazardous.o3: Pour it into the paint drum.
gloss.c.hazardous.w: Unknown products can react with others. Your supervisor knows where it can go safely.
gloss.w.balenpers: the baler (a machine that presses waste into blocks)
gloss.w.baal: the bale (a pressed block of paper or plastic)
gloss.w.vulopening: the loading opening (where the waste goes in)
gloss.s.baler.1: The press is stuck. Push the emergency stop.
gloss.s.baler.2: Never put your hand into the press.
gloss.c.baler.q: The press is jamming. May I take a look?
gloss.c.baler.a: No. First the power goes off.
gloss.c.baler.b: A baler presses with a huge force. Only use it when you have learned how. Never put a hand, an arm or a foot into the loading opening, also not when the machine looks still. Does it jam? Press the emergency stop, switch it off and make sure nobody can switch it on: follow the steps of your company. Only then look. Never climb into a baler or a container. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.baler.s: A piece of cardboard is stuck in the opening. The machine stands still. What do you do?
gloss.c.baler.o1: Switch it off fully, then take it out.
gloss.c.baler.o2: Pull it out quickly with your hand.
gloss.c.baler.o3: Push it in with your foot.
gloss.c.baler.w: A machine that stands still can start again. Without the power off, your hand is in danger.
gloss.l.shovel: The wheel loader on the yard
gloss.w.shovel: the wheel loader (a big machine with a bucket in front)
gloss.w.zwaailamp: the flashing light (an orange light on top of a machine)
gloss.w.bunker: the bay (a big concrete space for one kind of waste)
gloss.w.looppad: the walkway (a path only for people)
gloss.s.shovel.2: The wheel loader is reversing. Careful!
gloss.s.shovel.3: The flashing light is on. The machine is moving.
gloss.c.shovel.q: May I walk past the wheel loader?
gloss.c.shovel.a: Only if the driver sees you.
gloss.c.shovel: Stay out of the loader’s way
gloss.c.shovel.b: A wheel loader is big, and its driver sees little around it, especially behind it. So stay on the walkways, and wear your high-visibility clothes. Never walk behind a moving machine. Want to pass? Wait until the driver has seen you and gives a sign. The flashing light means: this machine is working. Keep visitors far away from it. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.shovel.s: You must walk past a working wheel loader. The driver looks the other way. What do you do?
gloss.c.shovel.w: A driver who has not seen you cannot stop for you.
gloss.w.zindelijk: potty-trained (the child can use the toilet)
gloss.s.nappies.1: I am going to change Sem.
gloss.s.nappies.2: Wash your hands after changing a nappy.
gloss.s.nappies.3: Never leave a child alone on the changing table.
gloss.c.nappies.a: At ten. It is in the app.
gloss.c.nappies.b: Get everything ready before you put a child on the changing table: a clean nappy, wipes and clothes. Then keep one hand on the child at all times. Never walk away, also not for a second. Wash your hands after every change, and clean the table. Write down when you changed the nappy, so the parents know. Do you see a rash or a wound? Write it down, and tell a colleague. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.nappies.s: You are changing a baby. You forgot the wipes; they are across the room. What do you do?
gloss.c.nappies.o2: Get them quickly: it is close.
gloss.c.nappies.o3: Leave the baby, and call out.
gloss.c.nappies.w: A baby can roll off a changing table in one second. Never leave a child alone up there.
gloss.s.mealtime.1: Wash your hands before the meal.
gloss.s.mealtime.2: Give Lisa her bottle at twelve.
gloss.c.mealtime.a: No, he has an allergy. Look at the list.
gloss.c.mealtime: Check the list before you give food
gloss.c.mealtime.b: Before you give a child food or drink, check the list: some children have an allergy, others may not eat certain food for their health or their faith. Wash your hands and the children’s hands before eating. Let children sit down while they eat and drink, never walk or run. Cut food small for small children, like grapes in pieces. Never give a child something from home of another child. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.mealtime.s: A child cries for a biscuit. You do not know this child well. What do you do?
gloss.c.mealtime.o2: Give it: it is only a biscuit.
gloss.c.mealtime.w: A biscuit can hold nuts, milk or egg. For a child with an allergy, that can be very dangerous.
gloss.w.bedje: the cot (a small bed for a baby)
gloss.s.naptime.1: Lay the baby on its back.
gloss.s.naptime.2: I often look into the bedroom.
gloss.s.naptime.3: Here is your cuddly toy. Sleep well.
gloss.c.naptime.a: Yes, since one o’clock. I will look again soon.
gloss.c.naptime.b: A baby sleeps safest on its back, in a sleeping bag, in its own cot. No pillow, no loose blanket and no big toys in the cot. Keep the room cool and fresh. Check sleeping children often: look and listen, also when the baby monitor is on. Does a parent ask you to let their baby sleep in another way? Tell your supervisor first. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.naptime.p: I will go and look in the bedroom.
gloss.c.naptime.s: A baby has fallen asleep on its tummy in the cot. What do you do?
gloss.c.naptime.o1: Gently turn it onto its back.
gloss.c.naptime.o2: Let it sleep: it is asleep now.
gloss.c.naptime.o3: Put a pillow next to it.
gloss.c.naptime.w: On its back, a baby can breathe freely. A pillow can cover its face.
gloss.s.playtime.1: We are going to play outside. Coats on!
gloss.s.playtime.3: One child at a time on the slide.
gloss.c.playtime.q: May I play with the puzzle?
gloss.c.playtime.a: Yes, at the table. Then you tidy it up.
gloss.c.playtime.b: Children learn by playing, so let them try things. But always keep them in sight, also outside. Count the children when you go out and when you come back in. Check the playground first: is the gate closed, is there glass or rubbish? Toys with small parts are not for children under three: they can choke on them. Clean toys that go in the mouth often. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.playtime.s: You come back in from the playground. You count one child too few. What do you do?
gloss.c.playtime.o1: Tell a colleague, and search at once.
gloss.c.playtime.o2: Wait: the child will come in by itself.
gloss.c.playtime.w: A child alone outside can get hurt or walk away. Every minute counts.
gloss.w.schriftje: the notebook (for notes between parents and staff)
gloss.w.ouderapp: the parent app (for photos and messages to parents)
gloss.w.wennen: to settle in (to get used to a new place)
gloss.s.pickup.1: I will write it in the notebook.
gloss.s.pickup.3: I am putting a photo in the parent app.
gloss.c.pickup.q: Who is picking Sem up today?
gloss.c.pickup.a: His grandma. She is on the list.
gloss.c.pickup: Only to people on the list
gloss.c.pickup.b: Give a child only to a parent, or to someone the parents have told you about. Do you not know the person? Ask who they are, look at their ID, and check with the parents or your supervisor. At pick-up, tell the parent how the day went: eating, sleeping, playing, and anything special. Write important things in the notebook or the app. Speak about other children only with their own parents. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.pickup.p: Who are you? I will call the parents.
gloss.c.pickup.s: A man you do not know comes to pick up Sem. He is not on the list. What do you do?
gloss.c.pickup.o1: Call the parents before Sem goes.
gloss.c.pickup.o2: Let Sem go: he knows the name.
gloss.c.pickup.o3: Ask Sem if he knows him.
gloss.c.pickup.w: You are responsible for the child until a person the parents chose takes over.
gloss.w.vingerstrip: the finger guard (on a door, so fingers do not get stuck)
gloss.w.verslikken: to choke (food goes the wrong way)
gloss.s.childsafety.2: I am putting some ice on the bump.
gloss.s.childsafety.3: Sem is choking. I am helping him.
gloss.c.childsafety.a: Yes, she has a bump. I am calling her mother.
gloss.c.childsafety: Look around with a child’s eyes
gloss.c.childsafety.b: Small children put everything in their mouth and climb on everything. So keep the stair gate closed, put cleaning products and medicines out of reach, and keep hot drinks away from children. Check the room every day. Does a child get hurt? Give first aid, comfort the child, tell the parents, and write it down. Is it serious? Call 112. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.childsafety.s: You put your hot coffee on a low table. A toddler walks to it. What do you do?
gloss.c.childsafety.o1: Put the coffee up high at once.
gloss.c.childsafety.o2: Tell the toddler not to touch it.
gloss.c.childsafety.w: Hot coffee can burn a small child badly. Out of reach is the only safe place.
gloss.w.huiduitslag: the rash (red spots on the skin)
gloss.w.adrenalinepen: the adrenaline pen (a medicine pen for a strong allergy)
gloss.s.sickchild.1: Sem has a fever. I am calling his father.
gloss.s.sickchild.2: Look at the allergy list before the meal.
gloss.s.sickchild.3: Never give a medicine without permission.
gloss.c.sickchild.a: He is very warm. I am going to take his temperature.
gloss.c.sickchild: A sick child: tell, do not guess
gloss.c.sickchild.b: Watch how the children are. Is a child hot, very tired, vomiting, or does it have a rash? Take its temperature, tell your colleague, and call the parents. Give a medicine only with written permission of the parents, and write down what you gave and when. Know which children have an allergy, and where their medicine is. A child with a strong allergic reaction: give the adrenaline pen if you have learned it, and call 112. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.sickchild.p: Your child is ill. Can you come and pick him up?
gloss.c.sickchild.s: A mother says: "Give him a fever drink at two." There is no form. What do you do?
gloss.c.sickchild.o1: Ask her to sign the form first.
gloss.c.sickchild.w: Without written permission you may not give medicine. The form protects the child and you.
gloss.w.mentor: the mentor (the worker who follows one child closely)
gloss.w.vierogenprincipe: the four-eyes rule (another adult can always see or hear you)
gloss.w.observeren: to observe (to watch carefully, and write it down)
gloss.w.peuter: the toddler (a child of two or three)
gloss.w.groep: the group (the children who are together every day)
gloss.s.grouprules.2: A colleague can always see or hear us.
gloss.c.grouprules.q: May I go outside alone with the group?
gloss.c.grouprules.a: Yes, but tell a colleague first.
gloss.c.grouprules.b: In child care, another adult must always be able to see or hear you when you are with the children. That protects the children and you. Every child has a mentor: one worker who follows that child closely and talks with the parents. Are you worried about a child at home, for example bruises or fear? Do not ask the child too much: tell your supervisor, who knows the steps. Rules differ per company: ask your supervisor what the rules are where you work.
gloss.c.grouprules.p: I am worried about this child.
gloss.c.grouprules.s: You see bruises on a child again. The child is quiet. What do you do?
gloss.c.grouprules.o1: Tell your supervisor the same day.
gloss.c.grouprules.o3: Call the parents and ask why.
gloss.c.grouprules.w: Your supervisor knows the steps for worries about a child. Many questions can scare the child.
